nodes.label: Minimal Agent SDK (examples/agent, Ledger::Client)
nodes.rationale: Single-file Ruby with no Rails dependency, plus JSON Schemas and a canonicalization test vector so third-party clients can confirm they hash identically.

nodes.label: Tasks::BuildContext (Context Compiler)
nodes.rationale: Deterministic, no LLM: same inputs give the same packet bytes excluding timestamps and signature.

nodes.label: eir-result-v1 result envelope
nodes.rationale: The signature covers the canonical envelope minus the signature field. No floats appear: the previous draft's self-reported extraction_confidence is removed because it is unverifiable, trivially gamed and unused by scoring.

nodes.label: eir-task-v1 task packet
nodes.rationale: Server-built, server-signed canonical JSON with a 500-2,500 token context budget; excerpts from a single source are capped to limit copyright exposure and prompt-injection surface.

nodes.label: idempotency_key
nodes.rationale: sha256(signer_key_id | task_id | payload_hash); a duplicate submission returns the original contribution and creates nothing.

nodes.label: Result ops
nodes.rationale: Ops use the same shape as the corresponding contribution action payloads; new objects may be referenced by a client-chosen ref string.

nodes.label: Quarantine reason categories
nodes.rationale: Closed list: PRIVATE_INDIVIDUAL, PERSONAL_DATA, UNLAWFUL_CONTENT, UNLICENSED_MATERIAL, SPAM. Disagreement with a claim or its politics is never a quarantine reason.

nodes.label: Analyze text page
nodes.rationale: Paste text, the stub proposes claims, the user edits/splits/types each with atomicity warnings and a private-individual checkbox, then optionally creates verification tasks.

nodes.label: Scenario I - Visible moderation
nodes.rationale: A PRIVATE_INDIVIDUAL quarantine hides the text but leaves a stub with moderator key, date and reason; an old snapshot still records that the claim existed.

nodes.label: Private-individual claims out of scope
nodes.rationale: A public ledger of scored assertions about identifiable private people is a defamation and privacy hazard; claim creation requires a checkbox affirmation and moderators can quarantine violations.

nodes.label: Claim Atomicity
nodes.rationale: Splitting exposes that 'the survey shows' is three textual claims, the causal link is a separate much weaker claim, and the recommendation is a value judgment. POC validation is a heuristic warning, not a hard block.

nodes.label: Contributor note fields are never included in any packet
nodes.norm_label: contributor note fields are never included in any packet
nodes.rationale: Notes are free text from untrusted parties and are the easiest injection path between agents.

nodes.label: Prompt Injection defenses
nodes.rationale: Server side: closed-enum ops, display-only HTML-escaped notes excluded from scoring, packets and summary inputs, excerpts labeled untrusted_excerpt, and scoring never reads text. Client side: delimit excerpts as data and give research agents minimal tool permissions.

nodes.label: Server-side hash chain (entry_hash / prev_hash)
nodes.rationale: Built server-side around the client signature because clients sign asynchronously and cannot know the previous log entry. Appends serialized with pg_advisory_xact_lock so seq is gap-free.

nodes.label: Transparency Log
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/log streams entries so third parties can mirror and verify the chain; the head hash can later be anchored externally. No blockchain.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/log
nodes.rationale: Raw log entries for mirroring; the complete P0 export.

nodes.label: Required Test Areas
nodes.rationale: Security and scoring tests matter more than UI tests.

nodes.label: Scenario J - Replay
nodes.rationale: Drop projections and caches, replay, and claim_score_digest for every pinned snapshot is unchanged.

nodes.label: The log comes first
nodes.rationale: The previous draft built graph tables in Phase 1 and added signed contributions in Phase 3; retrofitting a log under an existing CRUD model is the most expensive mistake available here. Each phase ends with green CI and no phase starts until the previous one's acceptance tests pass.

nodes.label: Stage 6 - Snapshots, score cache, and score endpoints
nodes.norm_label: stage 6 - snapshots, score cache, and score endpoints

nodes.label: claim_scores is a pure cache
nodes.rationale: Keyed by claim, seq and model and deletable at any time; a cache hit rebuilds the result from the stored trace so it reproduces the same bytes as a recomputation, which is what makes the byte-identical-after-wipe and after-replay tests meaningful.

nodes.label: Incremental recompute keyed by affected claims
nodes.norm_label: incremental recompute keyed by affected claims
nodes.rationale: Scoring::Affected derives the claims a contribution touches and the job is enqueued with after_all_transactions_commit so it runs after the enclosing transaction including the auto-ACCEPT appended inside it; key-management and model-release actions enqueue nothing.

nodes.label: Admin endpoints authenticated by a signed body
nodes.norm_label: admin endpoints authenticated by a signed body
nodes.rationale: Pins and recomputes are not log entries, so eir-admin-v1 carries the signer key, a timestamp within five minutes and an Ed25519 signature over the canonical body from a moderator key, keeping an operational power outside the log without making it anonymous.

nodes.label: Signed checkpoints on pinned snapshots
nodes.rationale: Snapshots::Create signs {protocol, node_url, node_key_id, seq, entry_hash, previous_checkpoint_seq, created_at} with the system key over canonical JSON, verifiable against any public key. created_at makes checkpoints non-deterministic across nodes, which is right: a checkpoint is a node's statement at a time, not a projection, so graph_snapshots is not a projection table and not in the replay digest.

nodes.label: The score cache is an N+1 and was 70% of the report
nodes.norm_label: the score cache is an n+1 and was 70% of the report
nodes.rationale: Scoring::Score.call opened with a find_by per claim per model — about 6,000 round trips for a whole-graph report, nearly all missing because the head seq moves with every append. The report paid a query to learn nothing, then computed anyway. Scoring::Score.call_many asks the cache once for the whole set; the computation is untouched and the spec asserts the trace and its hash are byte-identical to scoring one claim at a time (Invariant 4).

nodes.label: A query-count ceiling in the acceptance tests
nodes.norm_label: a query-count ceiling in the acceptance tests
nodes.rationale: A live record_investigation on this corpus was observed issuing 21,543 queries in one request, and a naive exporter over ~250 claims would be worse and would hold a request open for minutes. So the builder batch-loads by design, scores through Scoring::Score.call_many at a fixed seq, and renders to a file as a job — with a stated ceiling, because this is the place an N+1 hides best and hurts most.

nodes.label: The constitution page renders the bytes the hash covers
nodes.norm_label: the constitution page renders the bytes the hash covers
nodes.rationale: GET /constitution renders CONSTITUTION.md itself, the bytes the published constitution_hash covers, parsed and converted at render time, so what a visitor reads is what the hash certifies and no spec file had to be edited; the footer carries the constitution version and hash on every page.

nodes.label: /about and /licenses — what build is running and under what terms
nodes.norm_label: /about and /licenses — what build is running and under what terms
nodes.rationale: Revision, repository, node address and key, log head, released models, moderator keys, data licence, and the constitution version and hash — Article XIX applied to the software itself. A REVISION file written at image build wins over git. Drop-downs use details/summary rather than a menu library: no dependency, works without JavaScript.

nodes.label: Article VI Mapping — Constitutional States to Spec Representation
nodes.norm_label: article vi mapping — constitutional states to spec representation
nodes.rationale: Maps the constitution's named unknown-states onto INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, UNRESOLVED, model_dependent, NOT_APPLICABLE with reasons; underdetermined and observationally indistinguishable are question-level and deferred to P1.

nodes.label: Review Coverage as an Executable Checklist
nodes.norm_label: review coverage as an executable checklist
nodes.rationale: Coverage cannot measure 'most of the evidence that may exist', so it is shown only as 'N of M checks' and never as low/medium/high — a high label would read as the claim Article VIII warns against.

nodes.label: Known Gap — Extraordinary Evidence Not Modeled (flat priors)
nodes.norm_label: known gap — extraordinary evidence not modeled (flat priors)
nodes.rationale: ledger-default@0.1.0 uses the same 0.50 prior for ordinary and extraordinary claims, so Article XXIV is satisfied only in its 'well-audited' half. Recorded as a gap rather than hand-tuning priors, because whoever sets a prior class holds real power over outcomes.

nodes.label: Reading Order and Precedence
nodes.rationale: Read either the numbered files or FULL-SPEC.md, never both, because duplication invited an agent to read everything twice and drift.

nodes.label: AI Coding Agent Handoff
nodes.rationale: Names the precedence order, the invariants, the required artifacts and the success standard, so a coding agent can start without re-deriving the project's commitments.

nodes.label: Constitutional Compliance Map
nodes.rationale: Records where each Article is realized and at what tier (P0/P1/Partial/Gap). A row marked Gap is a known accepted shortfall, not permission to drift further.

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Applied to the v3/v4 Revision
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test applied to the v3/v4 revision
nodes.rationale: The residual risks named honestly: the system-key holder remains an open governance question, and moderation power is mitigated by visibility and appeals rather than eliminated.

nodes.label: Amendment 1.0.0 — Initial Adoption
nodes.rationale: Articles I–XXV adopted as written; only editorial additions (precedence header, shall/should definitions, scope, and the rule requiring Constitutional Test answers to be recorded for sensitive features).

nodes.label: Constitution Amendment Log
nodes.rationale: Append-only; every entry follows Article XXV's five-part format and each adopted entry is also recorded as an AMEND_CONSTITUTION contribution carrying the new constitution_hash.

nodes.label: Epistemic Ledger POC — README
nodes.rationale: Describes how the POC realizes the constitution; the constitution itself remains authoritative and is read first.

nodes.label: prior_class for Extraordinary Claims (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Gives whoever sets it real power over outcomes; needs a governance decision first.

nodes.label: Invariant 13 — Shared and Personal Stay Separate
nodes.norm_label: invariant 13 — shared and personal stay separate
nodes.rationale: Nothing user-specific or opinion-shaped is written to the log except as an ordinary evidence-bearing contribution.

nodes.label: Invariant 8 — Reputation Is Audit-Derived and Not a Scoring Input
nodes.norm_label: invariant 8 — reputation is audit-derived and not a scoring input
nodes.rationale: Task- and domain-specific, and deliberately stronger than Article X requires: reputation does not enter claim scores at all in v0.1.

nodes.label: When Uncertain — Simplest Reversible Option
nodes.rationale: Choose the simplest reversible option that preserves the invariants, record it, and continue; stop only when a requirement is impossible or two requirements cannot both hold. Never 'fix' a golden value to make something pass.

nodes.label: Article I — Claims Are Not Truth
nodes.norm_label: article i — claims are not truth
nodes.rationale: The system stores claims as objects of evaluation; nothing becomes true by endorsement, AI authorship, prestige, institutional support, consensus, or a high model score.

nodes.label: Article VI — "Unknown" Is a Valid Conclusion
nodes.norm_label: article vi — "unknown" is a valid conclusion
nodes.rationale: Inability to reach a conclusion is not a system failure; false certainty is.

nodes.label: Article VIII — Evidence Coverage Is Separate From Confidence
nodes.norm_label: article viii — evidence coverage is separate from confidence
nodes.rationale: A claim may have high modeled probability and low evidence coverage; both must remain visible.

nodes.label: Article X — Reputation Measures Reliability, Not Authority
nodes.norm_label: article x — reputation measures reliability, not authority
nodes.rationale: Reputation is task- and domain-specific and audit-derived; worldview, ideology, affiliation, popularity or conformity must never confer epistemic authority.

nodes.label: Article XV — Shared Evidence and Personal Belief Are Separate Layers
nodes.norm_label: article xv — shared evidence and personal belief are separate layers
nodes.rationale: Personal belief must not silently modify the shared evidence layer, yet a user should be able to explain what they believe and why without it masquerading as the system's assessment.

nodes.label: Article XVI — Disagreement Should Be Localized
nodes.norm_label: article xvi — disagreement should be localized
nodes.rationale: The goal is not forced consensus but intelligible disagreement: naming the three assumptions at issue beats declaring one side wrong.

nodes.label: Article XVII — Normative Claims Must Not Be Disguised as Empirical Facts
nodes.norm_label: article xvii — normative claims must not be disguised as empirical facts
nodes.rationale: Assigning fake empirical truth probabilities to moral or value judgments manufactures the appearance of precision.

nodes.label: Article XXIII — No Conclusion Is Immune From Re-Examination
nodes.norm_label: article xxiii — no conclusion is immune from re-examination
nodes.rationale: Remain open to correction without becoming vulnerable to endless evidence-free denial; challenges bear the same burden of provenance.

nodes.label: Article XXIV — Efficient Skepticism
nodes.rationale: Skepticism has value only when it can engage evidence; extraordinary conclusions require correspondingly strong and well-audited evidence.

nodes.label: Article XXV — The Constitution Itself Is Amendable, But Not Silently
nodes.norm_label: article xxv — the constitution itself is amendable, but not silently
nodes.rationale: The project should never drift into a different epistemic philosophy through undocumented implementation choices, so amendments are explicit, versioned, justified and preserved.

nodes.label: Constitutional Test
nodes.rationale: Ten questions asked before any major feature; a 'no' to 1, 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9, or a 'yes' to 3 or 4, requires written justification or a design change. Adopted because Article XXV's ban on silent drift had no enforcement point.

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q2 — Does it make disagreement more inspectable or less?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q2 — does it make disagreement more inspectable or less?

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q3 — Does it increase hidden authority?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q3 — does it increase hidden authority?

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q4 — Does it allow reputation to substitute for evidence?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q4 — does it allow reputation to substitute for evidence?

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q5 — Does it preserve uncertainty?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q5 — does it preserve uncertainty?

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q7 — Can an opposing investigator challenge it using the same system?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q7 — can an opposing investigator challenge it using the same system?

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q9 — Does it preserve the distinction between shared evidence and personal belief?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q9 — does it preserve the distinction between shared evidence and personal belief?

nodes.label: Constitutional Precedence Rule
nodes.rationale: The constitution outranks every other file; a conflict is recorded in 13-constitutional-compliance.md as a known gap or resolved by explicit amendment under Article XXV, never silently.

nodes.label: Node Reputation Is Operational, Not Truth Authority
nodes.norm_label: node reputation is operational, not truth authority
nodes.rationale: Uptime and protocol compliance must never become 'this node's claims are more true because the node is prestigious'.

nodes.label: Personal Belief Remains an Overlay
nodes.rationale: Federation synchronizes shared epistemic objects, not private beliefs.

nodes.label: P-3 — Designations of "Unknowable" Are Themselves Claims
nodes.norm_label: p-3 — designations of "unknowable" are themselves claims
nodes.rationale: Without this, labeling a claim untestable could shield it from evidence — the evidence-free denial Article XXIII warns against, pointed the other way.

nodes.label: P-4 — Strength of Evidence for Extraordinary Conclusions
nodes.norm_label: p-4 — strength of evidence for extraordinary conclusions
nodes.rationale: Posed as a question, not text: an auditable prior_class would hand whoever sets it real power over outcomes, so the spec takes option (a), accepting flat priors as a v0.1 limitation.

nodes.label: Coverage Became a Four-Item Checklist
nodes.rationale: 'Reviewed surface over estimated surface' had no data source; a checklist derived purely from the log does.

nodes.label: Reputation Removed from v0.1 Scoring
nodes.rationale: Scores depended on unrelated audit history, and a Beta(2,2) prior silently halved every new contributor's evidence, contradicting 'new contributors are not assumed malicious'.

nodes.label: Experiment 3 — Audit multiplier
nodes.rationale: Useful accepted contributions divided by audits plus corrections required; a configuration below 1 costs more than it helps, which is the test for whether an agent is worth running at all.

nodes.label: Connected assistants over MCP and OAuth
nodes.norm_label: connected assistants over mcp and oauth

nodes.label: record_investigation: one call records the whole check
nodes.norm_label: record_investigation: one call records the whole check

nodes.label: Every /api/v1 route is described in Api::Openapi
nodes.norm_label: every /api/v1 route is described in api::openapi
nodes.rationale: The suite fails on any route the document omits and on any described path that is not routed, so an endpoint and its documentation land in the same commit and the public API reference cannot drift.

nodes.label: Guidance: operational rules on the wire, not in the skill
nodes.norm_label: guidance: operational rules on the wire, not in the skill
nodes.rationale: A skill is installed once and never re-read, so a rule written there is frozen until every user reinstalls. Guidance is served on every MCP tool result and at GET /api/v1/guidance, so a change reaches a connected assistant on its next call; tool descriptions are cached and must never be a rule's only home.

nodes.label: Invariant 18: Galedra runs no model
nodes.rationale: The only Llm::Adapter is a deterministic stub. Any function needing a model (extraction, summary, deduplication, review) becomes a task or a tool for a connected assistant whose answer is a signed contribution open to audit; the server's only outbound requests are Stage 17 source fetches.

nodes.label: Article X — Reputation Measures Reliability, Not Authority
nodes.norm_label: article x — reputation measures reliability, not authority

nodes.label: Article XI — Identity Does Not Replace Evidence
nodes.norm_label: article xi — identity does not replace evidence

nodes.label: Article XIV — Humans and AI Are Contributors, Not Oracles
nodes.norm_label: article xiv — humans and ai are contributors, not oracles

nodes.label: What Claude must not do without explicit approval
nodes.norm_label: what claude must not do without explicit approval
nodes.rationale: Irreversible account-level actions — purchasing cloud services, changing production DNS, destroying infrastructure, deleting backups, rotating the system key, exposing PostgreSQL — require explicit authorization; infrastructure preparation in the repository does not.

nodes.label: Expensive AI work must stay off the central server
nodes.norm_label: expensive ai work must stay off the central server
nodes.rationale: A matter of principle before cost: the server only issues task packets, verifies signatures, validates schemas, appends, projects, audits, rescores, settles reviews and serves. Research runs on contributor machines and connected assistants, which keeps hosting cheap and matches the volunteer-network design.

nodes.label: Agents are contributors, not arbiters
nodes.rationale: An agent leases a signed task packet with the smallest sufficient context and returns a signed result validated server-side. Reputation tracks audited reliability at specific tasks in specific domains and deliberately does not enter claim scores in v0.1, so it can never become authority.

nodes.label: 06 §6 — Counts by state, no ranking, no score for a speaker
nodes.norm_label: 06 §6 — counts by state, no ranking, no score for a speaker

nodes.label: Stage 20 — Sections and placements in the log (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 20 — sections and placements in the log (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Sections are organizational rather than epistemic, but they are shared structure many principals add to over weeks and the public reads a speech through them, so filing must be attributed, replayable and reversible. Stage 15's TAG_CLAIM set the precedent. Two alternatives were rejected: sections as SOURCE_LOCATION rows (a subject is not one range of a recording) and a tree outside the log (a volunteer's placement arrives inside a signed TASK_RESULT and would have nowhere signed to land).

nodes.label: Stage 22 — Sharing and following an outline (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 22 — sharing and following an outline (implemented)
nodes.rationale: The link posted for a checked speech should be as useful as the link for a checked meme, and someone who wants to help should be able to find the big jobs. An outline's investigation reads its claims live rather than from a frozen claim_ids list, so the shareable page follows the work.

nodes.label: Article XVIII — Political Neutrality Is Structural
nodes.norm_label: article xviii — political neutrality is structural
nodes.rationale: Neutrality arises from consistent process, not artificial equivalence between unequal evidence; no aggregate political winner scores.

nodes.label: P-6 — Money Buys No Part of the Record
nodes.norm_label: p-6 — money buys no part of the record
nodes.rationale: Article XII names commercial capture but says nothing about the money that keeps a node running. The harm here is not a rewritten entry, which the log would expose, but an unrecorded arrangement that never touches the log at all; naming every sponsor applies Article XII's rule against silence to funding.

nodes.label: The share line — one line a person can paste
nodes.norm_label: the share line — one line a person can paste
nodes.rationale: record_investigation takes the exact statement the person wanted checked and creates an Investigation row — an index over log content, like receipts — with a public page and a 1200x630 PNG. The probability appears only in the permitted form ("0.9800 under ledger-default@0.1.0 at snapshot 412"); "accurate" and "% true" are refused because Article XXII forbids presenting a computed probability as a property of reality.

nodes.label: No probability, headline or badge for a section, source or speaker
nodes.norm_label: no probability, headline or badge for a section, source or speaker
nodes.rationale: A speech is never given a score, only counts by assessment state rolled up from children, and the fixed note "counts depend on extraction granularity" travels with every rendering and JSON. Investigations::Verdict and Cards::StatementImage refuse a section; a root's share card is its counts.

nodes.label: PLACE_CLAIM — filing is not certifying
nodes.rationale: Accepted on validation for any principal, because a placement changes no score and is reversible by INVALIDATE, so Article XI is untouched. A claim born in a section is one contribution; inside a TASK_RESULT the placement counts only when the result does.

nodes.label: No per-speaker counts inside one transcript
nodes.norm_label: no per-speaker counts inside one transcript
nodes.rationale: Article XVIII: sections may be named by speaker, but no count is broken out by speaker, because a per-speaker tally is a speaker score by another name.

nodes.label: The outline share line, fixed and without an adjective
nodes.norm_label: the outline share line, fixed and without an adjective
nodes.rationale: "Checked in Galedra: <heading> · N claims recorded, M checked · <states in 06 §6 order> · <url>" — counts in the spec's order and no adjective for the whole, because a speech is never given a verdict.

nodes.label: Large sources: record the structure first, then ask
nodes.norm_label: large sources: record the structure first, then ask
nodes.rationale: Galedra so far took a meme or a paragraph. When the whole check will not fit in about a quarter of an hour, the assistant records the structure (source, nested outline, one extraction task per leaf) so other volunteers can take the work in pieces, then asks whether to start on the research itself. Split into three tags so each leaves the demo goldens, replay and verify unchanged and can be reviewed alone.

nodes.label: Outline, section, root, leaf, placement — the fixed vocabulary
nodes.norm_label: outline, section, root, leaf, placement — the fixed vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Fixed once so no synonym appears anywhere: an outline is a tree of sections over one source; a root section has no parent, a leaf none below it, and a claim is placed in a section by a placement. Not "chapter", "topic" (taken by Stage 15), "collection" (reserved by 14 for federation), "folder" or "dossier".

nodes.label: A fallacy is not a refutation, attaches to a passage, and is not a ruling
nodes.norm_label: a fallacy is not a refutation, attaches to a passage, and is not a ruling
nodes.rationale: An argument can be badly made and its conclusion still true, so the page says so where the note is and no note changes a state, probability or trace. The anchor is a quoted, hashed SourceLocation, never a person, so what is described is exactly the text. And one assistant's opinion is model output, which Invariant 7 says is never evidence by itself, so a note reaches the page only once independent principals agree. Article XVIII is the reason to be strict rather than cautious: fallacy labelling is a standard partisan weapon.

nodes.label: 14 §24 — POC non-goal: do not build federation
nodes.norm_label: 14 §24 — poc non-goal: do not build federation

nodes.label: Stage 23 — Federation readiness (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Not federation: 14 §24 forbids peer discovery, consensus, sharding and replication here. The single node keeps the properties 14 §25 lists so a later federation stage finds nothing to undo. Each of the four gaps is one column or one small service, and none changes what a client signs, so every existing signature, hash and golden still verifies.

nodes.label: Stage 24 — Admins, help, and navigation (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Admin is not a ledger role. The log already holds its powers, all signed and public; admin is about accounts and menus, which live outside the log, so it is a column on users with who granted it and when. Built together with Stage 23 on the owner's instruction.

nodes.label: Stage 35 — Provenance is not corroboration (implemented, golden, default)
nodes.norm_label: stage 35 — provenance is not corroboration (implemented, golden, default)
nodes.rationale: Confirming a transcript faithfully records what a speaker said establishes provenance: the quotation is real. It says nothing about whether the speaker was right. An EVIDENCE_VERIFICATION task on an outline hands the worker the very sentence the claim was extracted from, and confirming it was scored as SUPPORT: 24 of the episode's 29 directional claims were supported only by the episode itself, so readers were shown "Checks out so far" where nothing outside the podcast was consulted — persuasion produced by accident.

nodes.label: Article XIX — Transparency Over Persuasion
nodes.rationale: A user should be free to reject the default assessment while still inspecting exactly how it was produced.

nodes.label: create_outline — source, one location per leaf, one CREATE_SECTION, one extraction task per leaf
nodes.norm_label: create_outline — source, one location per leaf, one create_section, one extraction task per leaf
nodes.rationale: Anonymous like record_investigation, so no token is needed to start a big job. A 60-leaf outline is about 62 writes, and the packet carries the locator, heading and anchor as untrusted_excerpt so the volunteer reads the range in the source itself: Galedra never fetches. The reply's `next` is the exact sentence to say, ending in the question whether to start on the research now.

nodes.label: contributors.home_url — a key says which node it lives on
nodes.norm_label: contributors.home_url — a key says which node it lives on
nodes.rationale: REGISTER_KEY accepts an optional plain http(s) origin, validated in the applier and projected; null means this node. Existing keys need no backfill, so nothing already signed changes meaning.

nodes.label: Ledger::Node — this node's identity is the system key
nodes.norm_label: ledger::node — this node's identity is the system key
nodes.rationale: No separate node key: the key at seq 0 already signs every entry, so a mirror learns the node's key from the log itself. Published as `node` in /api/v1/meta with address, key id, envelope and schema versions, checkpoint protocol, data licence, visibilities in use and the software build.

nodes.label: contributions.visibility — the node's statement, not the signer's
nodes.norm_label: contributions.visibility — the node's statement, not the signer's
nodes.rationale: A column on the log table and deliberately not part of the signed envelope: what a node may show is the node's statement, not the signer's. PUBLIC is the only value; a change of visibility remains a signed control entry (QUARANTINE, TAKEDOWN), and the app's DB role cannot UPDATE it.

nodes.label: The existing goldens prove nothing about the new rule
nodes.norm_label: the existing goldens prove nothing about the new rule
nodes.rationale: All 20 cases scored identically under 0.2.0 and 0.1.0, which is not a coincidence to wave at: the demo corpus contains no self-origin evidence and no duplicated passage, so the two things this model changes never arise. A separate provenance suite was added to both implementations — reference_scorer.py and the Ruby spec — with no code shared, and the expectations were reasoned before they were run. Seven of eight predicted fields were right; the eighth was wrong and the scorer was right.

nodes.label: Independence groups by origin AND passage, not origin alone
nodes.norm_label: independence groups by origin and passage, not origin alone
nodes.rationale: The first cut keyed ungrouped evidence by origin, which collapsed every passage of one document into a single group and dropped a qualifier that a supporting line then outranked — a qualifier and a supporting sentence from one report are not each other repeated. Keying on origin plus excerpt_hash makes the same passage entered twice count once while two genuine passages stay distinct. A spec caught it.

nodes.label: One origin per source, derived, without merging rows
nodes.norm_label: one origin per source, derived, without merging rows
nodes.rationale: Three URIs accounted for seven Source rows, and independence groups by evidence origin, so one URL being several rows let the same origin count twice — the double counting Invariant 6 forbids. Deriving a lineage key from the normalised canonical_uri at read time changes only the grouping: rows stay, nothing is mutated retrospectively, and two recordings of one URL remain two honest records by different people of one origin.

nodes.label: Affiliations::Resolve (alias-then-similarity lookup)
nodes.rationale: Named in the file header as the consumer: it maps a request through the alias table before trying similarity.

nodes.label: Affiliation group: Generation
nodes.rationale: Options carry explicit birth-year ranges in their labels so a person picks a cohort rather than supplying a date of birth.

nodes.label: Topic: Religion
nodes.rationale: Theology, scripture, and church history are kept as a distinct top level specifically so they stay separate from empirical claims rather than being scored as if they were.

nodes.label: Affiliation alias table
nodes.rationale: Owner request, 2026-09-19. Short forms and synonyms people actually type (gop, phd, zoomer, uk) are mapped to existing option slugs before any similarity matching is attempted, so a request for something the closed vocabulary already holds resolves exactly rather than fuzzily. Keys are normalized to lower case letters, digits and single spaces; values are option slugs from config/affiliations.yml.

nodes.label: Self-declared affiliations
nodes.rationale: Owner request, 2026-09-19. What a person says about themselves, so that in aggregate Galedra can show how different groups agree or disagree on a claim. Closed vocabulary, several groups, any number of picks, none required. Kept private to the account and shown only as counts, and only when a group is large enough (PersonalAssessments::MIN_GROUP) — the disclosure threshold is what makes an identity-revealing attribute safe to collect. Adding an entry is a code change reviewed like any other. Affiliations live outside the log and never reach scoring.

nodes.label: Active Storage — Content Hash Is Identity
nodes.norm_label: active storage — content hash is identity
nodes.rationale: sources.content_hash identifies the content and the blob key does not, so moving storage providers must not change any hash.

nodes.label: Background Jobs — Idempotent and Keyed by (target, seq)
nodes.norm_label: background jobs — idempotent and keyed by (target, seq)
nodes.rationale: So a retry or a replay never double-applies; recompute is incremental over only the claims whose counted links, evidence or groups changed at that seq.

nodes.label: Likely Future Hotspots
nodes.rationale: Scoring and recompute fan-out is the first candidate for extraction; task scheduling stays in Rails until measured otherwise.

nodes.label: Projection Concern — Validity Windows and active_at(seq)
nodes.norm_label: projection concern — validity windows and active_at(seq)
nodes.rationale: Rows carry created_seq and invalidated_seq and are readonly outside Ledger::Apply, which is what makes reproducing an earlier snapshot a query rather than a reconstruction.

nodes.label: Topology — Two Containers, Postgres for Everything
nodes.norm_label: topology — two containers, postgres for everything
nodes.rationale: Solid Queue and Solid Cache live in PostgreSQL so development needs exactly two services and no Redis.

nodes.label: Caching — Explicit Rows, Not Redis
nodes.rationale: The real caches are claim_scores and summaries rows that can be deleted at any time and regenerated.

nodes.label: Distributed Research, Centralized Coordination
nodes.rationale: Inference runs on contributors' hardware or accounts while the server does cheap deterministic work, so research throughput grows fast while central cost grows slowly.

nodes.label: Go vs. Rust (if ever)
nodes.rationale: Go for service-shaped concurrent database-heavy work, Rust for CPU-bound or untrusted binary parsing. There is no requirement that either is ever introduced.

nodes.label: Operational Goal — One Modest VM
nodes.rationale: Grow by pushing research compute outward before scaling anything central.

nodes.label: PostgreSQL, No Graph Database
nodes.rationale: Recursive CTEs, indexed edge tables, JSONB, full-text search and pg_trgm are enough for the POC and likely well beyond; pgvector only in P1 and only if trigram dedup proves inadequate.

nodes.label: Decision — Build the POC as a Rails 8.x Monolith
nodes.norm_label: decision — build the poc as a rails 8.x monolith
nodes.rationale: Not because Ruby is fast, but because the epistemic domain model will change repeatedly as real evidence graphs expose weaknesses, and familiarity decides how quickly bad abstractions and subtle bugs get noticed. This file is the single home for stack rationale.

nodes.label: Article XXI — Research Should Be Cumulative
nodes.norm_label: article xxi — research should be cumulative
nodes.rationale: An agent should not rediscover work another agent already did correctly; transient inference becomes persistent knowledge structure.

nodes.label: Claude MCP connection and identity choice
nodes.norm_label: claude mcp connection and identity choice
nodes.rationale: Three ways in: GALEDRA_URL/mcp anonymous, GALEDRA_URL/mcp/connect with OAuth where the person chooses once between signing in (so writes are attributed) and continuing anonymously, or a token from GALEDRA_URL/assistants/new sent as a Bearer header or embedded in the URL path for clients that cannot send headers.

nodes.label: Galedra as an epistemic ledger (skill definition)
nodes.norm_label: galedra as an epistemic ledger (skill definition)
nodes.rationale: The one-paragraph definition every connected assistant is given: a signed, append-only record of claims, the evidence bearing on them, where that evidence came from, and what has happened to it since. Explicitly not a source of truth — it gives traceable reasons for believing or doubting a claim. The negation is stated first so an assistant does not present a score as a verdict.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/guidance (non-MCP hosts)
nodes.rationale: REST hosts fetch the same rules at the start of a Galedra task, optionally narrowed with ?topic=. Assistants are told to fetch again in a later session rather than relying on memory, because a remembered rule has the same staleness problem as an installed one.

nodes.label: guidance object on every MCP tool result
nodes.norm_label: guidance object on every mcp tool result
nodes.rationale: Every MCP tool result carries a version, a topic and the text of the rules for the work being done. Nothing caches a tool result, which is exactly why this channel is chosen: it is always current, and where it differs from the installed skill it wins.

nodes.label: Guidance topics: check, outline, inference, work, correct
nodes.norm_label: guidance topics: check, outline, inference, work, correct
nodes.rationale: check records what was read; outline handles a source too large for one check; inference records a reasoning step; work answers open tasks; correct revises what is recorded. The five topics partition the assistant's whole surface onto the ledger.

nodes.label: Search first (search_claims before recording)
nodes.rationale: Call search_claims (or GET /api/v1/claims?q=) with the key words; if an accepted claim already matches, report its card and URL and stop unless there is new evidence to add. Prevents the ledger accumulating duplicate claims, since only an accepted, reversible MERGE_CLAIMS can join them afterwards.

nodes.label: The three things people use Galedra for
nodes.norm_label: the three things people use galedra for
nodes.rationale: Break something seen on social media into checkable claims and record it, so a link to the record is shared instead of a rumour; send someone a claim link so they see the reasons rather than take anyone's word; and help the project by checking claims already recorded. An assistant asked what Galedra is for must say these three in plain words before listing tools — capability lists describe the API, not the point.

nodes.label: The `galedra:` trigger
nodes.rationale: A message that is just `galedra:` followed by text — a pasted post, a sentence about to be shared — means check this before I share it, record the whole statement, and end with the share line. A single prefix stands in for the whole instruction so the user never has to describe the workflow.

nodes.label: ChatGPT instructions variant
nodes.rationale: Same body as skills/galedra.md with a ChatGPT-specific opening: plugin setup at GALEDRA_URL/mcp/connect with OAuth, GALEDRA_URL/mcp without, developer mode on. Notes that Custom GPTs are retired, and that a surviving GPT can import GALEDRA_URL/api/v1/openapi.json as an Action instead — the same OpenAPI document that /docs/api renders.

nodes.label: Claude skill package (SKILL.md)
nodes.rationale: Built from skills/galedra.md by bin/rails skills:build. Frontmatter name galedra, with a description that triggers on 'check this in Galedra' or asking whether something is true before posting it.

nodes.label: Generic system prompt variant
nodes.rationale: For hosts with no skill or plugin mechanism: read at GALEDRA_URL/api/v1 (OpenAPI at /api/v1/openapi.json) and, with a connected assistant token as a Bearer header, record investigations at POST /api/v1/investigations; use MCP instead where the host speaks it.

nodes.label: The working rules live on the server, not in the skill
nodes.norm_label: the working rules live on the server, not in the skill
nodes.rationale: A skill is installed once and never re-read, so a rule written in it is frozen at whatever it said on installation day and correcting it would mean asking every user to reinstall — not realistic in production. The file therefore deliberately omits the operational rules and points at the server instead, so a change reaches a connected assistant on its next call.

nodes.label: Ledger.replaying? — enqueue on live append only
nodes.norm_label: ledger.replaying? — enqueue on live append only
nodes.rationale: The CREATE_SOURCE applier must enqueue a fetch on a live append but never while ledger:replay rebuilds the projections, or a rebuild would go out to the network; the job is idempotent per (source_id, created_seq) as well.

nodes.label: Stage 16 — OAuth for connectors (implemented)
nodes.rationale: OAuth adds attribution and never becomes a requirement: anonymous use stays exactly as it is. A person signs in once on Galedra's own consent page and every later call is attributed to them, with no token to copy.

nodes.label: Serving from home: allowed hosts, Thruster TLS, and the token in the URL
nodes.norm_label: serving from home: allowed hosts, thruster tls, and the token in the url
nodes.rationale: Rails answers 403 at any name but localhost, so LEDGER_ALLOWED_HOSTS extends config.hosts with /up excluded for the container health check; the production compose file puts the image behind Thruster for a Let's Encrypt certificate. The MCP token may travel in the URL because Claude.ai's connector screen accepts only a URL and no headers - the URL is then the secret, and tokens stay revocable.

nodes.label: Tokenless writes become anonymous assistants
nodes.rationale: A caller with no token becomes an anonymous assistant keyed to its address for the day, minted on first use, so the work is still signed, delegated, capped per source per day, sampled at the anonymous rate and labelled; raw custodied writes and token management still need a real token.

nodes.label: The API mints anonymous tokens only
nodes.norm_label: the api mints anonymous tokens only
nodes.rationale: Signed-in minting lives on the connect page so an account's key is never used without its session; the API token endpoint is rate limited by address, and because Rails fixes a limiter's cache store at class-load time the limits go through a delegator so a spec can swap in a memory store.

nodes.label: Assistant tokens live outside the log
nodes.norm_label: assistant tokens live outside the log
nodes.rationale: Like custodied_keys, assistant_tokens survives replay while the log holds the facts that matter - the agent's REGISTER_KEY, the principal's DELEGATE and any REVOKE_DELEGATION - so revocation in the log always wins over the token row; tokens are stored as SHA-256 digests and shown once.

nodes.label: permissions.direct_work on a delegation
nodes.rationale: Under 02 SS1.1a direct work by a delegated agent stays PENDING, which would have left every assistant write uncounted; a delegation may now carry direct_work: true so such work counts as the principal's own hand. The grant is a signed, visible, revocable contribution and the work is still sampled at the raised rate.

nodes.label: One plugin, the person decides (anonymous or attributed consent)
nodes.norm_label: one plugin, the person decides (anonymous or attributed consent)
nodes.rationale: The consent page no longer requires sign-in up front; an anonymous grant issues a fresh anonymous assistant key per grant, adoptable later, so one /mcp/connect plugin serves both attributed and anonymous use and reinstalling to switch is never needed.

nodes.label: One durable delegation per person per client
nodes.norm_label: one durable delegation per person per client
nodes.rationale: The durable fact stays in the log: the first grant mints one AssistantToken through Assistants::Connect (agent key, logged DELEGATE, daily cap), and every access token maps onto it, so the revocation path is the one that already exists. Owner decision: tokens and delegations do not expire (100 years); revocation is the only end.

nodes.label: galedra:read scope, enforced on writes
nodes.rationale: A connector may ask for read-only; REST writes then answer 403 INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE with the RFC 6750 challenge and MCP writing tools return a tool error naming the scope to reconnect with, so the refusal tells the assistant how to fix it.

nodes.label: Two MCP doors: /mcp anonymous-or-token, /mcp/connect 401 challenge
nodes.rationale: /mcp/connect answers 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata=… until a bearer is presented, which is the discovery hook ChatGPT and Claude.ai follow. A presented but invalid credential is refused on either door rather than falling through to anonymous use, so clients refresh instead of writing anonymously by accident.

nodes.label: list_tasks, next_task, submit_task, release_task
nodes.rationale: list_tasks needs no token so an assistant can say what needs doing before anyone connects; next_task returns the packet in plain form with an `answer_with` note; submit_task takes an answer in the investigation vocabulary with handles ("target" is the packet's claim, "packet" its source location) and Tasks::Answer translates it into ordered TASK_RESULT ops so every 04 §6 check runs unchanged.

nodes.label: assessment_state
nodes.rationale: The primary, human-facing result.

nodes.label: Non-Scored Claims
nodes.rationale: NORMATIVE, RHETORICAL and METAPHYSICAL return NOT_APPLICABLE but may still have linked premises displayed; the system assesses premises without pretending to settle non-empirical conclusions.

nodes.label: Why INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE is not 0.50
nodes.rationale: The previous draft left an evidence-free claim at its prior, so an unsupported claim would display as a coin flip; showing the prior as if it were an assessment violates principle 8.

nodes.label: Political Speech Rule
nodes.rationale: Never produce a speaker- or party-level truth score; a speech view shows descriptive counts by assessment_state with a note that counts depend on extraction granularity. No ranking, no comparison across speakers.

nodes.label: Finding 5 — No Rule Covers Copyrighted Material Embedded in a Source (OPEN)
nodes.norm_label: finding 5 — no rule covers copyrighted material embedded in a source (open)
nodes.rationale: The assistant reasoned past a written instruction to a better answer, which is luck, not design: a different assistant follows the rule and transcribes the lot.

nodes.label: Stage 28 — Export and import a claim, a topic, or an outline (planned, not started)
nodes.norm_label: stage 28 — export and import a claim, a topic, or an outline (planned, not started)
nodes.rationale: Planned, not built. Federation is not being built here, but a file is the smallest thing that delivers 14 §P1's mirrors and §P2's partial nodes: a mirror is a node that imported one. It is also the answer to a question the project cannot currently answer a contributor — can I have my work back, in a form that outlives this server? Work no one can carry out of the building is not cumulative (Article XXI).

nodes.label: Epistemic Diff
nodes.rationale: The P0 snapshot design — validity windows plus seq — already makes this a query rather than a new subsystem.

nodes.label: Invariant 3 — Append-Only
nodes.rationale: Accepted history is never silently rewritten; corrections are new contributions.

nodes.label: Article XIII — Corrections Do Not Erase History
nodes.norm_label: article xiii — corrections do not erase history
nodes.rationale: Users must be able to reconstruct what the system believed at a given time and why, so corrections supersede rather than delete.

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q8 — Can the history of the conclusion be reconstructed?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q8 — can the history of the conclusion be reconstructed?

nodes.label: Redaction and Legal Takedown Across Jurisdictions
nodes.norm_label: redaction and legal takedown across jurisdictions
nodes.rationale: The federation should never falsely claim byte-perfect replay where lawful deletion has made that impossible.

nodes.label: P-2 — Lawful Removal Is Visible
nodes.rationale: Article XIII forbids erasing contributions merely for being wrong, which does not address legally compelled removal. A visible tombstone can leak that something sensitive existed; accepted as the lesser harm compared with silent removal. Implemented as the TAKEDOWN action.

nodes.label: Full is mirrored, Compact is re-asserted by the importer
nodes.norm_label: full is mirrored, compact is re-asserted by the importer
nodes.rationale: A foreign contribution cannot join this node's chain: splicing someone else's entries would break ledger:verify for everyone. Full arrives with its original signatures, verifiable against the origin's keys, kept verbatim as mirrored entries. Compact carries no signatures, so attributing it to the named authors would be a forgery this system would then publish as fact; it therefore creates new local contributions signed by the importer with derived_from. The failure is silent and permanent — a graph full of claims apparently signed by people who never saw them — so acceptance test 5 exists to catch it.

nodes.label: Moderation is visible in the counts; the personal layer never leaves
nodes.norm_label: moderation is visible in the counts; the personal layer never leaves
nodes.rationale: Quarantined and taken-down material is not exported and counts.withheld says how many entries were held back with the log entry that did it — a silent gap would be worse than a visible one (Article XIII). Personal assessments, affiliations, users, sessions and tokens appear in neither profile (Article XV), asserted by a test rather than left as a convention.

nodes.label: request_feature — assistants can say what they could not do
nodes.norm_label: request_feature — assistants can say what they could not do
nodes.rationale: Recorded in the assistant's own words at the moment it fell short. The rows live outside the log because they are untrusted text; repeats within 30 days are counted on one row, ten a day per assistant, and only moderators see them. The assistant is told it can at three points: the tool list, a hint on every refusal, and the guidance on every result.

nodes.label: Bug reports, the sibling of feature requests
nodes.norm_label: bug reports, the sibling of feature requests
nodes.rationale: Outside the log like feature requests, repeats within 30 days counted on one row, filed by assistants through report_bug (ten a day) or by people from Help, signed in or not (five an hour per address); guidance says when to use it against request_feature.

nodes.label: Auditor eligibility and domains
nodes.rationale: An auditor needs at least 5 audits and a mean of 0.8; established tiers are ESTABLISHED, EXTERNALLY_VERIFIED and INSTITUTIONAL. Reputation is domain-specific: general, ancient_near_east, us_economics, defaulting to general.

nodes.label: Topic: Ancient history (domain override)
nodes.rationale: The only child in the vocabulary that overrides its parent's audit domain: history/ancient maps to ancient_near_east, the domain the scoring spec already defines, instead of inheriting history.

nodes.label: Topic: Economics
nodes.rationale: Scope: markets, work, prices, and business. Maps to the us_economics audit/reputation domain rather than a generic economics domain, matching the domains the scoring spec defines.

nodes.label: Topic: History
nodes.rationale: Scope: what happened, and what the sources say happened — the two are deliberately named separately.

nodes.label: Descriptive counts, never a speaker score
nodes.norm_label: descriptive counts, never a speaker score
nodes.rationale: 06 SS6 forbids scoring a source or its author, so the source page shows counts by assessment state with the note that counts depend on extraction granularity, and nothing is ranked.

nodes.label: Server-custodied signing for browser users
nodes.rationale: Sign-up registers a server-custodied key through the log and every UI write goes through Ui::Write, which signs an ordinary envelope with the user's unlocked key and appends it with custody SERVER, so the browser is not a special write path; the server-held-key badge makes the custody visible.

nodes.label: The number is rendered only on request
nodes.norm_label: the number is rendered only on request
nodes.rationale: A closed <details> still ships the probability in the HTML and the rack_test driver reads it, so the calculation card and the trace are rendered only when ?calculation=1 is present; the default claim page contains no probability at all, which is stricter than 06 SS4 rule 1 and testable without a browser.

nodes.label: Contribution action types (P0)
nodes.rationale: One contribution = one action type; TASK_RESULT may carry an ordered list of at most 20 ops applied atomically.

nodes.label: Control contributions
nodes.rationale: Take effect immediately on append if the signer is authorized at that seq; an ACCEPT does not itself need accepting, and an unauthorized control contribution is rejected rather than logged.

nodes.label: Epistemic contributions
nodes.rationale: Projection rows are created with accepted_seq = null and do not count until an ACCEPT references the contribution. There is no PROPOSED status; a proposal is a row with accepted_seq null.

nodes.label: Genesis and key bootstrap (seq 0)
nodes.rationale: seq 0 is a self-signed REGISTER_KEY for the system key, also pinned in deployment config; signer_key_id is authoritative and contributor_id is resolved from it.

nodes.label: UNREPRODUCIBLE_REDACTED
nodes.rationale: Traces that cannot be reproduced after a takedown are reported, never silently changed.

nodes.label: Append-Only Semantics
nodes.rationale: Never hard-delete; corrections are new contributions. The app's DB role has no DELETE/UPDATE grant on contributions except the cached current_status column.

nodes.label: TAKEDOWN redaction manifest
nodes.rationale: A legally compelled removal deletes payload, envelope and blob bytes but keeps the hashes so the chain still verifies; the removal itself stays publicly visible.

nodes.label: Abuse Handling and Moderation
nodes.rationale: Moderation is never silent: quarantined content leaves a public stub at the same URL with moderator key, date, reason category and appeal path, and scores changed by a quarantine say so in their trace. Moderator actions are auditable and appealable.

nodes.label: compromised_since
nodes.rationale: Contributions from a key after the declared compromise seq are automatically marked CHALLENGED and queued for audit; they keep counting only if audits confirm them.

nodes.label: Topic: Science
nodes.rationale: Scope: natural science, its methods, and its findings. Audit domain: science.

nodes.label: Relationship to Prior Art
nodes.rationale: Most primitives exist elsewhere; the novelty is the combination of signed agent work packets, atomic evidence records, explicit independence, audited task reputation and versioned reproducible scoring. Keep P0 relational (no RDF core) and treat prior art as export targets.

nodes.label: 09 §1 — Inferences and premises tables (deferred), CREATE_INFERENCE reserved
nodes.norm_label: 09 §1 — inferences and premises tables (deferred), create_inference reserved

nodes.label: Stage 25 — Inferences: recorded reasoning steps (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Asked for by the owner: "Is this system capable of registering an inference like 'because A, B, and C are true and D is false this implies E is true'?" It was not. A claim edge relates two claims and nothing joined several premises into one step, so a reader could not see which premise is the weak link or that two people reached E by different routes.

nodes.label: Unfinished outlines on the weaknesses page
nodes.norm_label: unfinished outlines on the weaknesses page
nodes.rationale: Article XXII: an outline whose leaves are extracted but fewer than a quarter of whose claims carry any counted evidence is a big job left half done, and should be visible as such rather than reading as a finished check.

nodes.label: One DERIVED_FROM claim edge per premise, in the same contribution
nodes.norm_label: one derived_from claim edge per premise, in the same contribution
nodes.rationale: So downstream_count, task priority and the existing edge display keep working without knowing inferences exist — the new object is added without a second graph to maintain.

nodes.label: The weakest premise, marked rather than computed into a number
nodes.norm_label: the weakest premise, marked rather than computed into a number
nodes.rationale: Inferences::View ranks premise states (supported 0 … contradicted 4) against the polarity the inference needs; a FAILS premise reading SUPPORTED is the weakest of all. No number is derived for the conclusion from its premises, and the section says so in one fixed sentence. `strained` inferences feed the weaknesses page.

nodes.label: The three ceilings: /weaknesses, claim_scores, and serialised writes
nodes.norm_label: the three ceilings: /weaknesses, claim_scores, and serialised writes
nodes.rationale: The failure is not storage or signatures. /weaknesses walks the whole graph and scores every claim under every released model (~36 ms a claim, unusable at 10,000); claim_scores is keyed on an exact seq and never pruned, so the cache already outweighs the log; and Ledger::Append's pg_advisory_xact_lock is a global write ceiling (~31/s) — correct, and it stays, because it is what makes the sequence gap-free and the chain unbroken.

nodes.label: bin/demo golden-value demo and replay check
nodes.norm_label: bin/demo golden-value demo and replay check

nodes.label: Article XVII — Normative Claims Must Not Be Disguised as Empirical Facts
nodes.norm_label: article xvii — normative claims must not be disguised as empirical facts

nodes.label: Repetition is not corroboration (independence groups)
nodes.rationale: Evidence sharing an upstream origin is grouped and only the strongest member counts, so four citations tracing to one survey of 400 people cannot look like four corroborations.

nodes.label: Canonical Conventions — Names, IDs, Snapshots, Enums, No Floats
nodes.norm_label: canonical conventions — names, ids, snapshots, enums, no floats
nodes.rationale: No synonyms anywhere: truth_score and belief_probability were naming drift that made the earlier spec ambiguous about what was being computed.

nodes.label: Finding 11 — The Write Path Degrades Under the Pass (OPEN, two problems)
nodes.norm_label: finding 11 — the write path degrades under the pass (open, two problems)
nodes.rationale: A query-count N+1 and a slow template need different fixes; recording them as one entry would have pointed the profiling work in one direction and missed half of it.

nodes.label: Finding 2 — Pages Issue Thousands of Queries at 255 Claims (OPEN)
nodes.norm_label: finding 2 — pages issue thousands of queries at 255 claims (open)
nodes.rationale: /weaknesses at 13.5 seconds is the worst of it: the page Article XXII exists to serve, unusable on a corpus one person made in an evening. The lesson about the watching: a filter that only matches the thing you are thinking about will tell you that thing is fine.

nodes.label: BigDecimal and Canonical JSON Are the Churn, and Not a Bug (WON'T FIX)
nodes.norm_label: bigdecimal and canonical json are the churn, and not a bug (won't fix)
nodes.rationale: Half the allocation is the decimals and the canonical trace that makes a score reproducible by hand. Worth reducing by scoring fewer claims, not by making scoring cheaper and less honest.

nodes.label: The Box Is Not the Ceiling (NO ACTION NEEDED)
nodes.norm_label: the box is not the ceiling (no action needed)
nodes.rationale: 162 MB a worker, flat across 300 requests; what costs is garbage collection from the churn, not residency.

nodes.label: Follow-Up — What the Cold Path Costs (PARTLY FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: follow-up — what the cold path costs (partly fixed)
nodes.rationale: About 24 queries a claim, flat as the corpus grows, from per-link quarantine, challenge, audit and independence lookups. The structural batching fix is a refactor of the path the whole project's correctness rests on, guarded only by the golden tests, so it is recorded as the next piece of work rather than attempted at the end of a session.

nodes.label: Method Note — A Profile That Does Not Defeat the Cache Measures the Cache (FIXED in the harness)
nodes.norm_label: method note — a profile that does not defeat the cache measures the cache (fixed in the harness)
nodes.rationale: Development's reloader, verbose query logs and log writes were a fifth of the samples, and the warm-up run populated the page's own cache.

nodes.label: Ruled Out — A Leak (NO ACTION NEEDED)
nodes.norm_label: ruled out — a leak (no action needed)
nodes.rationale: Recorded as a negative so nobody spends a day on it.

nodes.label: Graph::Presenter.claim Issues 37 Queries per Claim (OPEN)
nodes.rationale: Bounded by page size rather than corpus size, which is why it has waited.

nodes.label: Same-Day Correction — Warm and Cold Paths Were Conflated (APPLIED)
nodes.norm_label: same-day correction — warm and cold paths were conflated (applied)
nodes.rationale: The 70% figure describes repeated views at one snapshot, not the first view after an append; the score cache is a table, not Rails.cache, so a cold measurement has to clear both.

nodes.label: Score Cache N+1 — 70% of the Report (FIXED via Scoring::Score.call_many)
nodes.norm_label: score cache n+1 — 70% of the report (fixed via scoring::score.call_many)
nodes.rationale: The report paid a query to learn nothing and then computed anyway; batched into one query for the set and one chunked insert, with specs asserting the traces and hashes stay byte-identical so Invariant 4 is checked rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Profiling Run — The Weaknesses Page at 3,000 Claims
nodes.norm_label: profiling run — the weaknesses page at 3,000 claims
nodes.rationale: A 24-core workstation flatters every number, and the recommended droplet has a fraction of that; read these as the shape of the problem, not the capacity answer.

nodes.label: Profiler Log Convention
nodes.rationale: A timing on its own says almost nothing; a timing next to the one before it, at a stated corpus size, is evidence. Every finding carries a status updated in place, because a log that still reads as open after the work is done hides the ones genuinely still there.

nodes.label: Stage 32 — Speaking modern MCP as well as legacy (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 32 — speaking modern mcp as well as legacy (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Written down in Stage 31 as a cheap version bump, and that was wrong. 2026-07-28 is a modern revision with no initialize handshake at all: version in per-request _meta plus a header, no session, a mandatory server/discover, resultType on every result, -32022 for an unsupported version, and notifications on a subscriptions/listen stream. Dual-era is the target, not migration: claude.ai is a legacy client, and a legacy client against a modern-only server simply fails with no fall-forward.

nodes.label: Stage 26 — Capacity: seeding, profiling, and the pages that scan (planned, half built)
nodes.norm_label: stage 26 — capacity: seeding, profiling, and the pages that scan (planned, half built)
nodes.rationale: Status is in progress, not implemented: bench:seed, bench:report, the profiling harness, batched scoring, scores:prune, the tally index, a bounded /weaknesses and the load test are in; the acceptance run at 100,000 claims and the run against a real droplet are not. Nothing here changes what the ledger records or how a claim is scored — only how much of the graph a request touches.

nodes.label: Calibration from Resolved Claims and Forecasts
nodes.norm_label: calibration from resolved claims and forecasts
nodes.rationale: Each calibrated parameter set is a new model version, never an in-place retune.

nodes.label: Omission and Framing Analysis
nodes.rationale: Each represented as explicit claims and evidence, never as a bare label, because a label like CHERRY_PICKED is easy to abuse.

nodes.label: Invariant 4 — Deterministic, Versioned Scores
nodes.rationale: Same seq plus same model yields a byte-identical trace; scorer code changes require a new model version.

nodes.label: Extraction Contract and Policy
nodes.rationale: Do not extract because compiled languages feel serious or microservices are fashionable; consider it only when profiling shows sustained saturation and the savings exceed running another service. Any reimplementation must produce identical canonical traces on the golden fixtures.

nodes.label: Article III — Evidence and Interpretation Are Distinct
nodes.norm_label: article iii — evidence and interpretation are distinct
nodes.rationale: "A source contains statement X" is a different object from "X is factually correct"; collapsing them into one truth label destroys the distinction the system exists to preserve.

nodes.label: Article XXII — The System Should Reveal Its Own Weaknesses
nodes.norm_label: article xxii — the system should reveal its own weaknesses
nodes.rationale: Self-critique is a core function, not an optional feature: "what would most change this conclusion?" must be easy to ask.

nodes.label: An inference is never evidence and never touches a score
nodes.norm_label: an inference is never evidence and never touches a score
nodes.rationale: Article III: evidence is what a source says or a measurement shows; an inference is what someone concludes from claims. So it carries no weight in either released model, the trace does not mention it, and traces are byte-identical before and after. A later model version may propagate belief; that needs cycle handling and a dependency model, and a new model version, never a change to an existing one.

nodes.label: Per-request _meta selects modern, not the header
nodes.norm_label: per-request _meta selects modern, not the header
nodes.rationale: A legacy client sends MCP-Protocol-Version on every request after its handshake, so treating the header's presence as modern intent would have reclassified every connector already talking to this endpoint. A request with no _meta is served exactly as before, header or no header. An unknown version in _meta is an error, not a fallback: the first cut fell through to legacy and served shapes the client never asked for, and the acceptance test for -32022 caught it.

nodes.label: Header/body agreement is enforced, including Mcp-Name
nodes.norm_label: header/body agreement is enforced, including mcp-name
nodes.rationale: The transport mirrors method and params.name into headers so intermediaries can route without parsing the body; skipping validation would leave exactly the hole the headers introduce, a proxy rate-limiting or routing on the header while the server acts on the body. Base64 sentinel values are decoded before comparison.

nodes.label: Legacy results returned byte for byte untouched
nodes.norm_label: legacy results returned byte for byte untouched
nodes.rationale: `decorate` adds resultType and the per-response serverInfo only on the modern path, and the legacy initialize result is asserted field for field in the spec, because the cost of getting this wrong is every existing connector. The existing MCP request specs passing unchanged is the real test.

nodes.label: listChanged stays false, deliberately
nodes.rationale: Declaring a capability the server cannot honour is worse than declaring none: a client that trusts listChanged: true will never re-fetch, because it believes it will be told. GET /mcp is 405 and the server pushes nothing; a stream per connected client is a capacity question before it is a protocol one. It is also not worth much, since ttlMs: 0 already tells clients not to cache and the rules ride on every result.

nodes.label: Bench::Isolation — measuring the app, not the reloader
nodes.norm_label: bench::isolation — measuring the app, not the reloader
nodes.rationale: The reloader, verbose query logs and log writes were a fifth of the samples in the first profile and none of them exists in production. Profiling also swaps the page cache for a null store, so a page that caches its own answer is measured doing the work rather than reading yesterday's. A timing without the corpus and machine it was taken on is not evidence, so every run is written up under docs/profiler/.

nodes.label: An expression index on the envelope, not a denormalised column on the log
nodes.norm_label: an expression index on the envelope, not a denormalised column on the log
nodes.rationale: Contributors::Tally joins contributions to agent_delegations through envelope->>'delegation_id', which nothing indexed, so crediting an agent's work to its principal scanned the log. The delegation id lives inside the signed envelope, and denormalising it would add a column to the one table this project is most careful about. Measured cost to writes: none detectable.

nodes.label: Two recorded departures: bench:rss instead of derailed_benchmarks, pg_stat_statements deferred
nodes.norm_label: two recorded departures: bench:rss instead of derailed_benchmarks, pg_stat_statements deferred
nodes.rationale: derailed_benchmarks would have brought a dependency tree, a second way of booting the app and its own idea of a request, to answer a question /proc/self/status answers in twenty lines — and the twenty lines let the slope be taken over the second half of a run, which is what makes the number honest. pg_stat_statements needed a shared_preload_libraries change and a restart; without query-level attribution a load test produces numbers nobody can attribute, so it must be closed before the load test, not after.

nodes.label: A score cache may be discarded because a score is a pure function of the log
nodes.norm_label: a score cache may be discarded because a score is a pure function of the log
nodes.rationale: scores:prune keeps the head seq, every pinned snapshot and anything within KEEP_DAYS. Nothing epistemic is lost: a pruned row returns byte-identical, which is the only reason a cache may be thrown away at all, and the spec deletes the head's rows and rescoring to prove it.

nodes.label: Canonical vocabulary: no synonyms anywhere
nodes.rationale: Score fields, states, model names and enums are fixed strings shared by docs, code, API fields and UI copy; enums are validated against a closed list rather than Postgres enum types, and no floats appear in signed payloads because canonical JSON must hash identically.

nodes.label: Article XII — The System Must Resist Capture
nodes.norm_label: article xii — the system must resist capture
nodes.rationale: The project assumes powerful actors will eventually try to manipulate it, so the defenses are structural — cryptographic attribution, append-only history, open scoring models, public traces, independent audits, provenance, independence analysis, reproducible snapshots, adversarial review, and alternative models over the same evidence — rather than trust in the operator.

nodes.label: Article XX — Models May Change; Evidence Must Endure
nodes.norm_label: article xx — models may change; evidence must endure

nodes.label: Portability rule: no provider-specific identity
nodes.rationale: Primary keys are UUIDv7 or derived from the contribution that created the row; every entry carries its content and chain hash, and Stage 23 added node identity, home_url on every key, explicit visibility and signed checkpoints, so the epistemic object under a human-facing URL is portable between nodes.

nodes.label: No single-operator dependency
nodes.rationale: No contributor, company or original maintainer should be able to make continued access to the public commons depend on their continued operation; the licensing structure optimizes for a commons that can outlive its founder.

nodes.label: Deterministic, versioned, replaceable scoring
nodes.rationale: Same snapshot plus same model version yields a byte-identical result, down to a recomputable trace. Two models ship so they can be compared on the same graph; the UI reports '0.86 under ledger-default@0.1.0 at snapshot 212' to prevent a number reading as truth.

nodes.label: Action Cable adapters
nodes.rationale: async in development, test adapter in test, solid_cable in production with 0.1s polling and one day of message retention — the database-backed adapter keeps the no-Redis constraint.

nodes.label: Solid Cache configuration
nodes.rationale: Database-backed cache (database: cache in production) capped at 256 MB and namespaced per Rails env; the commented max_age hook is left in place for retention policies.

nodes.label: Solid Queue dispatcher and worker pool
nodes.norm_label: solid queue dispatcher and worker pool
nodes.rationale: One dispatcher polling every second in batches of 500, workers on all queues with 3 threads and JOB_CONCURRENCY processes; the same default block is used in every environment so background behaviour does not diverge between dev and production.

nodes.label: Solid Queue finished-job cleanup
nodes.rationale: Hourly batched clear with a sleep between batches so the cleanup does not contend with appending transactions.

nodes.label: Active Storage on local disk
nodes.rationale: Only Disk services are enabled (tmp/storage in test, storage locally). The S3, GCS and mirror stanzas are left commented out: P0 explicitly excludes any external service, so blob storage stays on the node's own disk.

nodes.label: One PostgreSQL database per environment
nodes.rationale: Spec 11 §2: one app, one database. Solid Queue, Solid Cache, Solid Cable and Active Storage metadata all live in the same PostgreSQL database rather than in separate stores, so the deployment stays two Docker Compose services with no Redis. Connection settings come from the environment (see .env.example).

nodes.label: Test checkout_timeout for the append-lock concurrency spec
nodes.norm_label: test checkout_timeout for the append-lock concurrency spec
nodes.rationale: The concurrency spec runs 50 appending threads against the pg_advisory_xact_lock append lock; the 60 second checkout timeout exists so those threads can wait for a pooled connection instead of failing the test for an unrelated reason.

nodes.label: Article II — Evidence Must Be Traceable
nodes.norm_label: article ii — evidence must be traceable

nodes.label: Article XIII — Corrections Do Not Erase History
nodes.norm_label: article xiii — corrections do not erase history

nodes.label: Article XXIII — No Conclusion Is Immune From Re-Examination
nodes.norm_label: article xxiii — no conclusion is immune from re-examination

nodes.label: Developer Certificate of Origin rather than a CLA
nodes.norm_label: developer certificate of origin rather than a cla
nodes.rationale: A DCO has low contributor friction, preserves contributor ownership, records provenance and avoids giving the owner unilateral relicensing rights; a CLA can be reconsidered if a governance or dual-licensing reason emerges.

nodes.label: Rights attestation in the contribution envelope
nodes.norm_label: rights attestation in the contribution envelope

nodes.label: Signed hash-chained contribution log
nodes.rationale: The log is the source of record so that dropping every projection table and replaying returns identical snapshot hashes and scores; gap-free sequence numbers make a snapshot addressable without trusting a timestamp.

nodes.label: 400 Bad Request page
nodes.rationale: Static, self-contained error page served without the Rails stack; noindex/nofollow and all CSS inline so it renders when the app cannot.

nodes.label: 406 Unsupported Browser page
nodes.rationale: Rails 8 serves this when a browser fails the allow_browser modern-browser check, so unsupported clients get a page instead of a broken Hotwire app.

nodes.label: robots.txt
nodes.rationale: Left at the Rails default comment only — nothing is disallowed, so the public record, including claim pages and the moderation log, stays fully crawlable.

nodes.label: Core Principles (implementation summary)
nodes.rationale: Sixteen principles condensed from the constitution, including 'determinism is not objectivity' and 'answers first, graphs underneath'.

nodes.label: Lessons From Prior Argument-Mapping Projects
nodes.rationale: Adoption fails on high contribution cost, benefits accruing to later users, readers wanting conclusions, and moderation and capture.

nodes.label: ClaimReview
nodes.rationale: Its reviewRating expects a verdict, which conflicts with model-conditional, no-verdict display; any use must be opt-in and carry state and model rather than a truth rating.

nodes.label: GALED
nodes.rationale: A naming collision with a very close metaphor; the reason not to use plain 'GalEd' as the public brand.

nodes.label: Kialo
nodes.rationale: Argument mapping; lessons about readers wanting conclusions and about moderation and capture.

nodes.label: Legal Citation Verification Market
nodes.rationale: A real market already paying for one-time citation checks; the lesson is which parts generalize outside legal research.

nodes.label: Nanopublications
nodes.rationale: Closest publishing-format precedent; assertion, provenance and publication-info graphs are the intended P1 export mapping.

nodes.label: Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG)
nodes.rationale: Possible source of structured candidate claims, evidence or identifiers.

nodes.label: Reason Commons
nodes.rationale: Philosophically the closest project found: it independently recognizes that useful reasoning disappears inside conversations and documents. Monitor closely as a potential collaborator.

nodes.label: Rootclaim
nodes.rationale: The closest precedent for the probabilistic layer, but oriented to producing an analysis, where the ledger preserves the reusable substrate from which many analyses can later be generated.

nodes.label: Scite
