nodes.rationale: Demonstrates that users value evidence-aware research tooling; citation-context classification is adjacent evidence, not an epistemic substrate.

nodes.label: W3C PROV
nodes.rationale: Contributions map to activities, agents and entities; export mapping planned for P1.

nodes.label: Wikidata
nodes.rationale: Could reduce ontology work through entity identifiers.

nodes.label: Research Notes — Adjacent Systems and Prior Art
nodes.norm_label: research notes — adjacent systems and prior art
nodes.rationale: No mature system was found combining all the core ideas into a general-purpose, agent-native, auditable epistemic substrate; several solve parts well and should be interoperated with rather than reinvented.

nodes.label: What the Demo Proves and What It Does Not
nodes.norm_label: what the demo proves and what it does not
nodes.rationale: It proves the mechanics but not that the weights are right; every relevance label and interpretive-step count is a judgment, shown being made explicitly, attributed, challenged and revised.

nodes.label: Standards Compatibility — PROV, Nanopublications, ClaimReview
nodes.rationale: ClaimReview needs care: its reviewRating expects a verdict, which sits badly with the model-conditional, no-verdict display rules, so any output is opt-in per record and carries state and model rather than a truth rating.

nodes.label: Invariant 16 — Answers First, Numbers on Request
nodes.norm_label: invariant 16 — answers first, numbers on request
nodes.rationale: The default claim view is the answer card; probabilities sit behind Show calculation.

nodes.label: Invariant 17 — Determinism Is Not Objectivity
nodes.rationale: Never describe a score as objective in UI copy, docs, or API field names.

nodes.label: Article VII — Probabilities Are Model-Conditional
nodes.rationale: A computed probability is never an objective property of reality; different scoring models may legitimately differ on the same evidence, so every score names snapshot, model, version, evidence and trace.

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q6 — Can the result be reproduced?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q6 — can the result be reproduced?

nodes.label: Evidence Can Be Shared Without Sharing Conclusions
nodes.norm_label: evidence can be shared without sharing conclusions
nodes.rationale: Nodes may agree about source, quotation, measurement and provenance while disagreeing about priors, models and final assessment; the federation should not require one global truth score. This is a feature, not fragmentation.

nodes.label: Product Bet (v4) — Make AI Research Cumulative
nodes.norm_label: product bet (v4) — make ai research cumulative
nodes.rationale: The POC does not bet on becoming a public truth network. It bets that AI agents increasingly do research that is expensive to repeat and hard to audit, so P0 must be useful to one person or team with no other contributors.

nodes.label: Determinism Does Not Eliminate Judgment
nodes.rationale: Judgment remains in wording, relevance, support strength, interpretive distance, independence grouping and priors; the response is not to hide the subjectivity but to make it explicit, signed, challengeable, versioned and auditable.

nodes.label: Long-Term Architecture Position — An Integration Layer
nodes.norm_label: long-term architecture position — an integration layer
nodes.rationale: Become an integration layer over Scite, Wikidata, OpenAlex, nanopublications and PROV rather than attempting to replace existing infrastructure.

nodes.label: Probabilities and Public UX
nodes.rationale: A bare 0.73 is read as '73% true', which is too strong; default presentation should lead with state, coverage, stability and the main unresolved issue, with the calculation in an advanced view.

nodes.label: Strategic Conclusion — Verified Once, Reusable Forever
nodes.norm_label: strategic conclusion — verified once, reusable forever
nodes.rationale: The differentiator is not that the system can check a citation, which many tools do, but that a successful verification becomes a durable epistemic object another person, document or agent can reuse and independently audit.

nodes.label: Working Conclusion — Do Not Sell the Check, Preserve the Check
nodes.norm_label: working conclusion — do not sell the check, preserve the check
nodes.rationale: Build the missing integration layer while reusing existing standards; turn disposable AI research into durable, independently auditable epistemic infrastructure.

nodes.label: Topic: Society
nodes.rationale: Scope: media, education, crime, and migration. Audit domain: society.

nodes.label: Topic: Politics
nodes.rationale: Scope: elections, policy, government, and international affairs. The scope line states the governing rule explicitly: claims, never speakers, are assessed. Audit domain: politics.

nodes.label: 03 §7 — A score is meaningless without its model and snapshot
nodes.norm_label: 03 §7 — a score is meaningless without its model and snapshot

nodes.label: AgentBad's False Verification (L10)
nodes.rationale: A verification that passes every server-side validation and is still false, caught only by audit — the demo's proof that validation is not correctness.

nodes.label: Finding 10 — The Queue Spends Its Effort on Claims Evidence Cannot Settle (OPEN)
nodes.norm_label: finding 10 — the queue spends its effort on claims evidence cannot settle (open)
nodes.rationale: 38 of the top 40 tasks by priority targeted NOT_APPLICABLE claims whose outcome is fixed before the check starts; closing the route to revising the type is tempting and probably wrong, because the type is itself a judgement.

nodes.label: Stage 30 — The whole text, readable in Galedra (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 30 — the whole text, readable in galedra (implemented)
nodes.rationale: A person reading an outline should be able to read the source: a leaf holds the text of its own passage, a branch composes its leaves, the root shows the whole transcript. The Moonshots outline had 35 anchors totalling 4,514 characters standing in for a multi-hour episode, and the page labelled an anchor "the passage this section covers", which is the misreading that prompted the stage.

nodes.label: Stage 34 — A person can finish their own investigation (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 34 — a person can finish their own investigation (implemented)
nodes.rationale: A person outlined a two-hour source into 247 claims over 1,679 signed writes, and all 742 verification tasks behind them were closed to them, so the outline read "182 unresolved" until a stranger arrived. That is a dead end for the only user the node has, and a bad trade: it protected a number nobody is reading yet at the cost of the product being finishable.

nodes.label: Stage 33 — Take an outline away as a file you can read (planned, not started)
nodes.norm_label: stage 33 — take an outline away as a file you can read (planned, not started)
nodes.rationale: Planned, not built. One run produced 62 sections, 47 leaves, 141,937 characters of readings, ~250 claims and ~780 open checks over ~2,500 signed contributions, and the only way to keep it is to keep the node running. Stage 28 exports JSON for machines and its hard problem is forgery; this exports a document for people and is deliberately a dead end. Offering only the second to someone asking for the first is the mistake the stage exists to avoid.

nodes.label: Invariant 5 — Unknown Is Explicit
nodes.rationale: NOT_APPLICABLE and INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE carry no probability anywhere; a directional state needs evidence in that direction.

nodes.label: Invariant 7 — AI Is Never Evidence By Itself
nodes.norm_label: invariant 7 — ai is never evidence by itself
nodes.rationale: MODEL_OUTPUT weighs 0; agent results are closed-enum ops that pass validation and remain auditable.

nodes.label: v4 Bug — Directional States Require Matching Evidence
nodes.norm_label: v4 bug — directional states require matching evidence
nodes.rationale: With a non-0.50 prior the v3 rule labeled a claim with only supporting evidence 'leans contradicted'; found while building the public demo (08 C6).

nodes.label: The size rule — outline first above roughly 3,000 words
nodes.norm_label: the size rule — outline first above roughly 3,000 words
nodes.rationale: An assistant never records a partial check as if it were whole. The server enforces what it can: a statement over 2,000 characters, or more than 40 new claims without sections in one bundle, is refused with a reply pointing at create_outline. The judgment itself lives in the guidance, because the server cannot measure whether the assistant read the sources.

nodes.label: Anchor versus reading — a cleaned transcript is not a quotation
nodes.norm_label: anchor versus reading — a cleaned transcript is not a quotation
nodes.rationale: The two must never be the same field. An anchor is the leaf's opening words verbatim, hashed and checked against the fetched source; a reading is the full text cleaned by an assistant, hashed over the cleaned text and never checked, displayed as an attributed, dated transcription. The moment an assistant fixes transcription errors, what it produces is a model's reading of the source, and model output is never evidence by itself. Collapsing the distinction would make Galedra a place where edited speech is attributed to real people with a hash beside it.

nodes.label: A branch composes its leaves, it does not store text
nodes.norm_label: a branch composes its leaves, it does not store text
nodes.rationale: Sections::Text walks the subtree in document order and assembles readings at read time, so there is exactly one copy of anything, a correction to one leaf corrects every level above it, and the composition stays derived (Invariant 2). The root's page is the whole transcript without a transcript ever being written twice.

nodes.label: The narrow cleaning rule (a speaker who misspeaks stays misspoken)
nodes.norm_label: the narrow cleaning rule (a speaker who misspeaks stays misspoken)
nodes.rationale: "Fix errors" is an invitation to rewrite, so the rule is deliberately narrow and negative: paragraphs where the speaker changes subject, misheard words, mangled proper nouns and punctuation, [unclear] for what cannot be made out, and nothing else. No tidying grammar, no removing repetition or filler, no summarising, no reordering, and no reconstructing from memory — the misspeaking is often the thing worth checking.

nodes.label: Retrieval excludes readings by identity, not by locator type
nodes.norm_label: retrieval excludes readings by identity, not by locator type
nodes.rationale: The obvious filter — stop checking TRANSCRIPTION locations — would break Stage 13's legitimate use, text an assistant read off an image, which should still be looked for. So the exclusion is by id, from the set of locations that are some section's reading. Reporting a reading as not found would report a failure that is not one, because it never was a quotation.

nodes.label: Tool results are the only channel with no staleness
nodes.norm_label: tool results are the only channel with no staleness
nodes.rationale: The skill is never re-read until a user reinstalls; initialize instructions are reportedly discarded by claude.ai; tool descriptions are cached from the last connection and reportedly truncated near 500 characters. Results are never cached, so every operational rule rides on them, each naming its topic and version; descriptions repeat only what survives truncation and are not what the code relies on.

nodes.label: The size rule's `or` limb — a rule that could not fire
nodes.norm_label: the size rule's `or` limb — a rule that could not fire
nodes.rationale: "Under 3,000 words of input, OR under about 25 claims" joined two limbs by `or`, and the second limb is the assistant's own output: deciding to record thirteen claims was what made recording thirteen claims permitted. A two-hour, fourteen-chapter transcript went through record_investigation as thirteen claims. The rule is now stated on the input alone.

nodes.label: Self-checks are filtered before the scorer, not flagged inside it
nodes.norm_label: self-checks are filtered before the scorer, not flagged inside it
nodes.rationale: Tasks::Checks.for excludes self-performed results so they never enter task_checks and cannot move review_coverage — the whole safety of the stage. A flag would change the shape of the scoring trace, and Invariant 4 then requires a new model version, new config, new goldens and a reference-scorer pass for a feature that must not move the number anyway. Excluding keeps every existing trace byte-identical.

nodes.label: Instructions describing behaviour the code no longer has
nodes.norm_label: instructions describing behaviour the code no longer has
nodes.rationale: The next_task description and Guidance::OUTLINE still said a principal never gets a check on its own claim, and the full suite passed against instructions that contradicted the code they described — the third time the project shipped a behaviour change while the thing an assistant reads kept describing the old one.

nodes.label: No free-standing accuracy rating; the task outcomes are the rating
nodes.norm_label: no free-standing accuracy rating; the task outcomes are the rating
nodes.rationale: The owner asked for "their own accuracy score", and the instinct is right, but a new rating would be the assistant's own judgement with a number attached — MODEL_OUTPUT, which Invariant 7 weighs at zero. The verification task outcomes are already a closed, server-validated enum with the reading behind them, so unlocking them gives what was asked and invents nothing.

nodes.label: self_performed recorded at lease time, never recomputed
nodes.norm_label: self_performed recorded at lease time, never recomputed
nodes.rationale: Deriving it later by comparing principals would change as keys are adopted and contributors merge; a fact about what happened must not be recomputed from a world that has since changed.

nodes.label: The share line names all three numbers
nodes.norm_label: the share line names all three numbers
nodes.rationale: "247 claims · 247 self-checked · 0 independently checked" rather than the shorter "none independently checked": it is what someone pasting the link is publishing about their own work, it states the weakness in the same breath as the volume, and it keeps reading correctly as the second number falls behind the third.

nodes.label: provenance_factor — a claim's own origin cannot support it
nodes.norm_label: provenance_factor — a claim's own origin cannot support it
nodes.rationale: A link is self-referential when its evidence's origin is an origin the claim was extracted from, derivable deterministically from placement→section→source against link→evidence→location→source. At SELF the weight is 0.0, exactly as MODEL_OUTPUT already is under observation_weight. The link is not discarded but kept, displayed and counted, because knowing a quotation is faithful is worth knowing; it simply stops being mistaken for corroboration.

nodes.label: The model is provenance and routing; it never touches a score
nodes.norm_label: the model is provenance and routing; it never touches a score
nodes.rationale: The dangerous reading is "work by a better model is better work", which Article XI, Invariant 8 and Invariant 7 all forbid — and a model name is a weaker signal than either, self-declared besides. It may decide who is offered a task and how often that work is audited; it may never change a probability, a state or a trace, and the scoring configs do not learn the field exists. Acceptance test 4 checks the goldens rather than trusting the reading.

nodes.label: Readings travel only when the source's licence says they may
nodes.norm_label: readings travel only when the source's licence says they may
nodes.rationale: An outline's readings are a transcription of someone else's work — ~142,000 characters of a commercial podcast in the run that prompted this — and a file is easier to redistribute than a page. The source `license` field is nil on every source today, so --readings stays opt-in, prints attribution and licence beside the text, and says the reading is a contributor's transcription rather than a licensed copy. The stage should not ship its default before the owner settles the policy.

nodes.label: An exported file must never read as more settled than the record
nodes.norm_label: an exported file must never read as more settled than the record
nodes.rationale: A static file outlives what it describes while the node moves on, so every export states on its face the snapshot seq and scoring model (03 §7: a number without both is meaningless, and a file is exactly where such a number goes to be quoted out of context), that it is a point-in-time copy with the live URL, and that claims are provisional until audited. It carries the plain headline, never a bare probability, and never says true or false.

nodes.label: Print-to-PDF rather than a PDF engine
nodes.norm_label: print-to-pdf rather than a pdf engine
nodes.rationale: The stack is settled and a PDF engine is a large dependency — a gem that renders its own layout, or a headless binary in the image. The HTML gets a real @media print stylesheet with page breaks at sections instead; adding an engine later is a separate decision with its own justification, and starting without one is the reversible choice.

nodes.label: Topic: Technology
nodes.rationale: Scope: software, hardware, AI, and security. Audit domain: technology.

nodes.label: Topic: Environment
nodes.rationale: Scope: climate, energy, and wildlife. Audit domain: environment.

nodes.label: Argument Compiler
nodes.rationale: Primary abstraction: compile a document into an auditable evidence graph rather than organize documents, citations or embeddings. Existing systems do not organize the atomic reasons for believing a claim.

nodes.label: Design Philosophy: make disagreement cheap and hidden assumptions expensive
nodes.norm_label: design philosophy: make disagreement cheap and hidden assumptions expensive
nodes.rationale: The log stores both 'E supports C' and 'it does not, because qualifier Q was omitted'; the scoring model resolves current weight by public, versioned rules.

nodes.label: Epistemic Intermediate Representation (EIR)
nodes.rationale: The compiler's persistent output format: atomic claims, evidence with exact provenance, support/contradict/qualify links, independence groups, deterministic scoring. Chosen so the reasoning behind an answer is reusable rather than re-derived by each agent.

nodes.label: Determinism is not objectivity
nodes.rationale: The scorer makes reasoning reproducible, not its inputs objective; relevance labels, interpretive-step counts, independence groupings, claim wording and observation types are judgment calls, so each is made explicit, attributed, challengeable, versioned and auditable.

nodes.label: Constitution Preamble: preserve the structure of inquiry
nodes.norm_label: constitution preamble: preserve the structure of inquiry

nodes.label: Reading order and spec precedence
nodes.rationale: The constitution outranks everything; among spec files the more specific wins. A spec instruction that would violate an Article is resolved by honoring the Article and recording the conflict in the stage file, never silently.

nodes.label: Rules for editing the spec
nodes.rationale: FULL-SPEC.md is generated and never hand-edited; a golden value is never changed to make something pass, because the reference scorer exists precisely to say which side is wrong.

nodes.label: Article XXV — The Constitution Itself Is Amendable, But Not Silently
nodes.norm_label: article xxv — the constitution itself is amendable, but not silently
nodes.rationale: An amendment must state what changed, why, what problem motivated it, what risks it introduces and whether it alters prior compatibility, so the project cannot drift into a different epistemic philosophy through undocumented implementation choices.

nodes.label: Article VI — "Unknown" Is a Valid Conclusion
nodes.norm_label: article vi — "unknown" is a valid conclusion

nodes.label: Article XXIV — Efficient Skepticism
nodes.rationale: Skepticism has value only when it can engage evidence, so the system distinguishes 'this claim is unsupported' from a refusal to accept any possible evidence, and 'unconventional' from 'contradicted by evidence'.

nodes.label: Unknown is a first-class result (INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE)
nodes.rationale: A claim with no counted evidence must report INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE rather than falling back to the prior, because a prior-derived direction would manufacture a verdict from nothing.

nodes.label: 04 §3.1 — Blind independent verification and no self-certification
nodes.norm_label: 04 §3.1 — blind independent verification and no self-certification

nodes.label: Stage 8 - Tasks, leases, packets, and the example agent
nodes.norm_label: stage 8 - tasks, leases, packets, and the example agent

nodes.label: Stage 27 — Model provenance and task routing (planned, not started)
nodes.norm_label: stage 27 — model provenance and task routing (planned, not started)
nodes.rationale: Planned, not built. A claim extraction over a long transcript needs a frontier model with a large context; deciding whether one quoted sentence supports one claim does not, and a 7B model on a local GPU could do that volume work for nothing. Today the ledger cannot tell the two apart, so it offers every task to everyone.

nodes.label: Stage 29 — Noting a logical fallacy (planned, not started)
nodes.norm_label: stage 29 — noting a logical fallacy (planned, not started)
nodes.rationale: Planned, not built. A meme can be factually unimpeachable and still be a straw man, so today the part of a statement that does the persuading passes unremarked. Described as the most easily abused thing yet proposed here: icons are read as verdicts.

nodes.label: Blind multi-assignment and its limit
nodes.rationale: Task reads hide results until all slots submit or leases expire with none live, but the public log itself is not blind, which 04 SS3.1 cannot fully achieve on a transparency log; the gap is recorded rather than papered over.

nodes.label: One signed packet per task
nodes.rationale: Blind multi-assignment (04 SS3.1) means literally identical packets, so the packet is built once at task creation and shared by every assignee and lease_expires_at lives on the assignment instead of inside the packet, a deviation from the 04 SS3 example that keeps one task_packet_hash per task.

nodes.label: Per-op semantic checks run inside the append transaction
nodes.norm_label: per-op semantic checks run inside the append transaction
nodes.rationale: Refs must resolve before the type-scope rules can be checked, so the checks run after resolution inside the transaction and a rejection rolls the whole append back: nothing is logged and no seq is consumed.

nodes.label: Acceptance is per result, not per claim
nodes.norm_label: acceptance is per result, not per claim
nodes.rationale: 04 SS4.3 says each extracted claim, but per-claim acceptance would need row-level ACCEPT, which 02 SS1.1a does not define; results that only add objects are system-accepted, while extraction results and anything superseding another principal's work stay pending for a different principal, as one contribution.

nodes.label: Agent sources are metadata-only and the server never fetches
nodes.norm_label: agent sources are metadata-only and the server never fetches
nodes.rationale: 04 SS6 step 9 forbids server-side retrieval of agent-supplied URLs, so a source created inside a task is stored retrieval_pending with no content or content hash, and CHAR_RANGE locations are refused on such sources until content is imported.

nodes.label: Tasks are operational tables, not projections
nodes.norm_label: tasks are operational tables, not projections
nodes.rationale: Task creation is not an action in the closed list, so replay leaves tasks and task_assignments alone; the consequence is that GET /log alone does not carry task targets, so task-derived review checks need the public task registry. Recorded for the owner as a gap in log self-containment.

nodes.label: No lease on a task standing on the leaser's own principal's say-so
nodes.norm_label: no lease on a task standing on the leaser's own principal's say-so
nodes.rationale: The first draft excluded anything the principal recorded and broke the public demo, where the verifier searches opposing evidence on a claim it extracted and the curator accepted. The narrower rule — recorded by that principal AND accepted by the system rather than by a different principal — keeps 08 §7 intact and still stops an assistant verifying the claim its own person just recorded.

nodes.label: INFERENCE_REVIEW task type, and the config it deliberately did not edit
nodes.norm_label: inference_review task type, and the config it deliberately did not edit
nodes.rationale: Deviation from the plan: the released scoring configs were not edited to add its task_type_cost, because a config change would be a new model version (Invariant 4). Tasks::Priority falls back to the type's own cost for a type the config predates. Outcomes VALID, MISSING_PREMISE, NON_SEQUITUR, CANNOT_DETERMINE; a MISSING_PREMISE answer adds a claim and a corrected inference and the original stays.

nodes.label: The code was stricter than the spec, so no amendment was needed
nodes.norm_label: the code was stricter than the spec, so no amendment was needed
nodes.rationale: 04 §3.1 forbids exactly two things — auditing your own contribution and accepting your own proposed claim — and neither is a task type. Tasks::Lease applied its self-authorship guard to every type, so EVIDENCE_VERIFICATION, OPPOSING_EVIDENCE_SEARCH and QUALIFIER_CHECK were blocked along with audits. That extra strictness, not the rule, is what made a solo investigation unfinishable.

nodes.label: single_model_dependence on the weaknesses page
nodes.rationale: The honest use of the field: a claim whose evidence rests entirely on work by one declared model, or entirely on UNKNOWN declarations, is a real weakness. Not to discount the work, but to say plainly what it rests on (Article XXII).

nodes.label: The envelope's `software` field exists and is unusable
nodes.norm_label: the envelope's `software` field exists and is unusable
nodes.rationale: Of 600 sampled contributions only 173 carry `software` at all; model_id was "oauth" 93 times, "unknown" 37, "none" 5 and a real identifier 26. The OAuth connect path writes a connection method into the field that should hold a model, nothing validates it, and no projection, index, query, page or routing reads it. An honest unknown is worth more than a wrong answer — the same rule the scoring model follows for INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

nodes.label: CREATE_INFERENCE — premises with polarity, type, rule, self-assessed strength
nodes.norm_label: create_inference — premises with polarity, type, rule, self-assessed strength
nodes.rationale: Two to twelve premises, each HOLDS or FAILS, with the warrant stated as untrusted display text and strength shown as a self-assessment. A conclusion among its own premises is refused; cycles across inferences are allowed and recorded because they are information (Article V), and no scorer ever follows them.

nodes.label: The closure — where a claim's file stops
nodes.norm_label: the closure — where a claim's file stops
nodes.rationale: The graph has no natural edge, so it must be decided before anything is written. Inference premises are referenced by id and not followed, or a single claim drags in the graph; an unresolved reference is marked external with its origin so a reader can tell a boundary from an omission.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/claims/:id/card
nodes.rationale: P1: compact JSON plus HTML fragment so integrations need no graph logic.

nodes.label: Distribution (P1+)
nodes.rationale: Adoption depends more on answers appearing where people already work - document editors, AI writing tools, browser extensions, internal knowledge tools - than on graph views.

nodes.label: Claim references - how often a claim is met
nodes.norm_label: claim references - how often a claim is met

nodes.label: Claim reference counts live outside the log
nodes.norm_label: claim reference counts live outside the log
nodes.rationale: A count is not an epistemic fact: claim_references is one row per claim, kind and day, counted by an upsert that never raises so a failed count cannot break the read or write it rides on, and it is not signed, not replayed and never reaches scoring. Crawlers inflate VIEWED and SHARED, so CHECKED and LOOKED_UP are the cleaner signals.

nodes.label: Ordered by how often a claim was met, never by how wrong it is
nodes.norm_label: ordered by how often a claim was met, never by how wrong it is
nodes.rationale: 06 SS4 rule 12 forbids ranking claims by wrongness and persuasive framing, so the owner's top-10-common-lies request is served as the references order with the state filter set to CONTRADICTED, in neutral wording, and will never be titled lies.

nodes.label: Article IV — Atomicity

nodes.label: Checking what is left of the usage limits
nodes.norm_label: checking what is left of the usage limits
nodes.rationale: Subagent-heavy sessions at large context dominate the budget, and a review that dies halfway leaves findings applied but unverified, which is worse than not starting it.

nodes.label: bundler-audit CVE ignore list
nodes.rationale: bin/bundler-audit checks every gem in the Gemfile against known advisories; CVEs judged not to apply are enumerated here rather than silently skipped, so each dismissal is visible in the repository.

nodes.label: audit_schedules
nodes.rationale: Storing the inputs as of evaluated_at_seq makes the sampling decision inspectable without replay and immune to later graph changes.

nodes.label: audits
nodes.rationale: An audit may target another audit's contribution (RE_AUDIT); the latest active audit on a target governs its effect.

nodes.label: reputation_events
nodes.rationale: Current reputation is computed from active events at a snapshot; nothing stores a mutable total.

nodes.label: provisional
nodes.rationale: Any counted link comes from a contribution not yet audited CONFIRMED; validation proves well-formedness and attributability, not correctness.

nodes.label: Appeals (RE_AUDIT)
nodes.rationale: If a re-audit disagrees, the first audit is invalidated and the target's rows are restored by a new ACCEPT with a new created_seq; history shows the gap.

nodes.label: Suspicious Contribution Clusters (P1)
nodes.rationale: Article XXII report on audit-failure rates by principal, model family, prompt version and time window; it raises audit rates through an anomaly factor and never invalidates anything by itself.

nodes.label: Scenario B - Poisoned contribution
nodes.rationale: Exists to demonstrate that validation is not correctness and that the provisional flag matters: a real excerpt passes automated checks, a sampled audit returns SUBSTANTIVE_ERROR, the link is invalidated, and the old snapshot still shows the poisoned state with its trace.

nodes.label: Extraordinary Claims (known gap)
nodes.rationale: Article XXIV asks that extraordinary conclusions require correspondingly strong evidence; v0.1 delivers the well-audited half but uses flat priors. Do not patch it by hand-editing priors; any fix must be an auditable, versioned model feature (proposed amendment P-4).

nodes.label: Audit input anchoring (v4 fix)
nodes.rationale: Every input is evaluated as of the contribution's own seq and stored in audit_schedules, so later audits, new edges or reputation changes cannot retroactively change whether an old contribution should have been sampled.

nodes.label: Model and Software Provenance
nodes.rationale: Recording software and delegation_id enables systemic-error audits like 'all links created by model X, prompt v1' and ensures no model family becomes a privileged source (Art. XIV).

nodes.label: Reputation Calculation (Beta-Binomial)
nodes.rationale: Per (contributor, task_type, domain) from active reputation_events. The prior changed from Beta(2,2) to Beta(1,1) because reputation no longer multiplies evidence and the display should not suggest a synthetic track record; mean is always shown with n and a 'limited history' label below n = 3.

nodes.label: Reputation roll-up to the principal
nodes.rationale: Closes the loophole where a principal could launder bad agent history by spinning up new agent keys; revoking a compromised agent does not erase failures before compromised_since.

nodes.label: Default English locale file
nodes.rationale: Still the stock Rails scaffold: the only key is hello. UI copy in this application is written in views and services rather than routed through I18n, so there is no domain vocabulary here.

nodes.label: Deferred scope
nodes.rationale: Documented in 09 and explicitly not built: inference/premise tables, entity resolution, forecast dual scoring, claim-to-claim propagation, pgvector, federation.

nodes.label: Non-Goals
nodes.rationale: Do not determine ultimate truth, build one universal probability model, arbitrate moral values, replace professionals, prevent all coordinated attacks, build a blockchain, index the web, or host copyrighted text.

nodes.label: Rails Guidance
nodes.rationale: UUIDv7 keys, service objects for anything crossing models, JSONB for evolving metadata, validated string enums rather than Postgres enum types because they change too often during a POC, projections read-only outside Ledger::Apply.

nodes.label: Agent Protocol goal
nodes.rationale: Agents are ephemeral workers attached to a durable substrate; the server cannot see or control an external agent's prompts, so every safety property is enforced server-side on what the agent returns.

nodes.label: Privacy
nodes.rationale: Contributors are never required to expose real name, location, employer or IP history; do not fingerprint, and store IPs only in short-retention request logs, never in the ledger. Pseudonymous reputation is a feature.

nodes.label: Ledger::Apply
nodes.rationale: The only writer of projections; a pure function of contribution plus current projections, so replay reproduces every row.

nodes.label: truth_evaluable
nodes.rationale: Defaults from the claim type and may be overridden only by a signed contribution; keeps non-empirical claims out of empirical scores.

nodes.label: claims
nodes.rationale: DISPUTED is removed as a status: disputation is a score property (contested), not a lifecycle state.

nodes.label: evidence_claim_links
nodes.rationale: note is display only; it is never fed to scoring or to other agents' prompts.

nodes.label: evidence_items
nodes.rationale: Evidence with no group is treated as its own singleton group and counted in the trace as independence_unreviewed.

nodes.label: source_locations
nodes.rationale: For CHAR_RANGE on stored text, excerpt must equal the stored slice and excerpt_hash must match.

nodes.label: sources
nodes.rationale: content_hash is independent of the storage backend; lineage_key suggests an independence origin.

nodes.label: Validity windows (created_seq / invalidated_seq)
nodes.rationale: A row is active at snapshot S iff created_seq <= S and (invalidated_seq is null or > S); links additionally need accepted_seq <= S to be counted.

nodes.label: Step 1 - Select counted links
nodes.rationale: Contributor reputation is deliberately not an input: weighting by reliability made scores depend on unrelated audit history, let a Beta prior silently halve every new contributor's evidence, and trusted self-reported agent confidence.

nodes.label: CLAIM_DEDUPLICATION
nodes.rationale: P1; output is candidate edges only, never merges.

nodes.label: Product Hypothesis (v4)
nodes.rationale: P0 must give one user or small team day-one value even if nobody else contributes; public argument-mapping systems stalled on contribution cost, moderation, cold start, and readers wanting answers not graphs. Sequencing only, not a data-model change.

nodes.label: TEXTUAL claim type
nodes.rationale: Added in v4 because the seeded demo, quote verification and sermon/legal use cases depend on claims about what a text contains, which behave differently from claims about what happened. Whether TEXTUAL stays a distinct type is reserved for the owner.

nodes.label: Claim identity (no text-uniqueness constraint)
nodes.rationale: The same proposition can be phrased many ways and small wording changes can change what evidence applies, so similarity only proposes candidate relationships; MERGE_CLAIMS is explicit, attributed, accepted and reversible by INVALIDATE.

nodes.label: The Log Is the Source of Record
nodes.norm_label: the log is the source of record
nodes.rationale: Event-sourced design chosen because the previous draft gave projection tables mutable status columns with no record of when they changed, making historical snapshots unreproducible.

nodes.label: Reputation - what it means
nodes.rationale: The audited, empirically observed rate at which an identity performs a specific task type correctly in a specific domain. It does not mean the identity's beliefs are likely true and in v0.1 does not influence claim scores; it drives audit sampling, task eligibility and display.

nodes.label: Search
nodes.rationale: P0 PostgreSQL full-text plus pg_trgm for near-duplicate suggestions; P1 pgvector. Similarity is used for discovery and deduplication only, never as evidence weight.

nodes.label: First Experiments (after P0 passes)
nodes.rationale: P0 proves the mechanics; these test the product hypothesis: claim identity, single-user value, audit multiplier (useful accepted contributions divided by audits and corrections required - below 1 costs more than it helps), answers without graphs, and independence impact.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/admin/recompute
nodes.rationale: Moderator-only: enqueue full recompute.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/admin/snapshots
nodes.rationale: Moderator-only: pin a label to a seq.

nodes.label: Contributor page
nodes.rationale: Per task type x domain: audited count, mean, limited-history label. No followers, likes or aggregate prestige.

nodes.label: personal_assessments
nodes.rationale: P1, reserved: personal lenses live outside the contribution log and never feed Ledger::Apply, scoring, packets or summaries (constitution Art. XV).

nodes.label: independence_reviewed
nodes.rationale: every counted evidence item has an independence group, or an accepted SOURCE_INDEPENDENCE_CHECK targets this claim

nodes.label: opposing_search_done
nodes.rationale: an accepted OPPOSING_EVIDENCE_SEARCH result targets this claim, even if it found nothing

nodes.label: primary_source_reviewed
nodes.rationale: a counted link exists from evidence whose source is PRIMARY_TEXT, DATASET, MEASUREMENT or LEGAL_DOCUMENT

nodes.label: qualifiers_reviewed

nodes.label: review_checklist
nodes.rationale: Declared per model; a release is rejected if a declared check cannot be satisfied by an available task type.

nodes.label: CLAIM_EXTRACTION

nodes.label: OPPOSING_EVIDENCE_SEARCH
nodes.rationale: Replaces 'contradiction search': it searches opposite to the claim's current lean, and a NONE_FOUND result still satisfies opposing_search_done because a documented null search is information.

nodes.label: QUALIFIER_CHECK
nodes.rationale: Promoted to P0 in v4 because the public demo depends on discovering an omitted qualifier; looks for omitted time ranges, populations, denominators, baselines, sampling limits, jurisdictions and translations.

nodes.label: SUMMARY_GENERATION
nodes.rationale: P1, external.

nodes.label: Phase 7 - Seeded Demo
nodes.rationale: bin/demo and the Watchers example must run on a clean database, print every golden value with PASS/FAIL, and exit non-zero on any mismatch.

nodes.label: Scenario A - Quote verification
nodes.rationale: TEXTUAL claim, agent verification CONFIRMED, claim SUPPORTED and provisional, reviewer audit clears provisional and raises verifier reputation.

nodes.label: Scenario D - Omitted qualifier
nodes.rationale: The qualifier check finds the survey sampled only customers; C2 becomes UNRESOLVED while the narrower C3 stays SUPPORTED.

nodes.label: Scenario G - Non-scoreable claim
nodes.rationale: A NORMATIVE claim gets NOT_APPLICABLE and no number, but its premises can still be linked and displayed.

nodes.label: Personal belief is never styled as an assessment
nodes.norm_label: personal belief is never styled as an assessment
nodes.rationale: Art. XV: P1 personal views appear in a separate labeled panel with their lens stated and never replace, average with, or sit in the headline position of the shared assessment.

nodes.label: Scale Expectations
nodes.rationale: The schema should not preclude ~100k claims, ~500k links, ~1M contributions; load testing is not required for the POC and premature optimization is discouraged.

nodes.label: Foundational Statement
nodes.rationale: The highest commitments are provenance, reproducibility, openness to correction, explicit uncertainty, inspectable disagreement and intellectual honesty — not consensus, authority or certainty.

nodes.label: Preamble — Preserve the Structure of Inquiry
nodes.norm_label: preamble — preserve the structure of inquiry
nodes.rationale: The purpose is not to declare official truth, enforce consensus, reward conformity or replace human judgment, but to make knowledge cumulative, disagreement inspectable, correction normal and uncertainty explicit.

nodes.label: Stage 15 — Topics (implemented)
nodes.rationale: A topic is a judgment about a claim, so it must be a signed, attributable, challengeable log entry rather than a column someone edits. The vocabulary is closed and two levels deep so filing is checkable, and each node names the audit/reputation domain it maps to so reputation stays per subject without a second vocabulary. Untagged claims stay in `general` rather than being unscorable (conservative reading).

nodes.label: Purpose before plumbing (three things a person does with Galedra)
nodes.norm_label: purpose before plumbing (three things a person does with galedra)
nodes.rationale: Asked what Galedra is for, Claude listed ten tools and their enums. The initialize instructions and the skill now open with the three uses; an empty search returns the total of accepted claims plus a note that the subject is more likely unrecorded than mis-searched, because Claude could not tell an empty ledger from a narrow search.

nodes.label: config/topics.yml closed topic vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Twelve top-level subjects with children, each naming the audit/reputation domain it maps to; kept as data rather than code so filing never invents a subject. Adding a topic stays a code change for now (reserved decision).

nodes.label: topics:backfill — system-signed guessed tags
nodes.rationale: Guesses are recorded as system-signed TAG_CLAIM entries whose note says they are guesses, and REPLACE=1 re-guesses only earlier backfills, never tags set by people or assistants, so a machine guess can never quietly overwrite a human judgment.

nodes.label: A declared model is a claim about itself, not a fact
nodes.norm_label: a declared model is a claim about itself, not a fact
nodes.rationale: An assistant says what it is and nothing verifies it, so the record stores and shows it as declared. A local 7B claiming to be a frontier model gets frontier tasks and fails its audits, which is what audits are for. UNKNOWN is the default tier and never an error — a fact about config/models.yml, not about the model — and UNKNOWN is offered SMALL work only, the same conservative reading the ledger applies wherever it does not know something.

nodes.label: config/fallacies.yml — a closed vocabulary including FALLACY_FALLACY
nodes.norm_label: config/fallacies.yml — a closed vocabulary including fallacy_fallacy
nodes.rationale: Data like config/topics.yml so adding one is not a code change; no free-text fallacy names ever. FALLACY_FALLACY is in the list deliberately, because it is the mistake the feature invites and should be as nameable as the rest. Two entries must say they overlap with what the ledger already measures: CHERRY_PICKING is what independence groups exist to expose, and APPEAL_TO_AUTHORITY is close to what Article X settles — a note that duplicates a measurement is weaker than the measurement.

nodes.label: Smaller Notes (FIXED)
nodes.rationale: None exploitable; each a habit worth not keeping — an interpolated quote rather than a bind, an interpolated table name, and a throttle that slept the whole minute regardless.

nodes.label: Finding — Server-Side Request Forgery by DNS Rebinding (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding — server-side request forgery by dns rebinding (fixed)
nodes.rationale: The checked address was discarded and the connection resolved the name a second time, so a short-TTL name answers public for the check and private for the connection. The recorded per-excerpt found/not-found result is an oracle against an internal endpoint, one guess at a time. Fixed by pinning Net::HTTP#ipaddr= to the address that passed the check, which leaves the Host header, SNI and certificate verification on the hostname.

nodes.label: Brakeman Warnings Dismissed (NOT EXPLOITABLE)
nodes.rationale: Each read at the source rather than taken on its confidence rating: normalized input that cannot carry a quote, a Date from a closed case, a constant CRC lock key, literal table names, and a URL validated at append.

nodes.label: What Held Up
nodes.rationale: Established by reading so the next audit need not re-derive it: injection, dynamic dispatch guarded by a frozen KINDS list, no cookie surface on the API, PKCE-only OAuth, digest-only tokens, authorization, output escaping, mass assignment and redirects.

nodes.label: Standing Rules Every Audit Checks
nodes.rationale: Drawn from the constitution and CLAUDE.md: the single write path, projections written only by Ledger::Apply, untrusted text inert, and the server's only outbound requests being source fetches — anything else making a network call is a finding in itself.

nodes.label: Review Notes — Changes Across Revisions
nodes.rationale: Records what was wrong or risky in the previous spec and what this revision does about it, ordered by impact; not required for implementation.

nodes.label: Security Audit — Full Application (2026-09-19)
nodes.rationale: Scope stated with what it left out — deployed configuration, the skill's prompt-injection surface, denial of service by expensive queries — because an audit that does not say what it left out invites the reader to assume it covered everything.

nodes.label: Security Log Convention
nodes.rationale: A finding investigated and dismissed is worth as much to the next reader as one that was fixed: it stops the same ground being covered twice and records why it was dismissed, which is the part that can turn out to be wrong later. A scanner warning is not a finding.

nodes.label: Scholarly Corpus Integration
nodes.rationale: Store references and provenance, do not redistribute restricted full text; server-side fetching needs an allow-listed sandboxed fetcher because of SSRF.

nodes.label: Invariant 1 — Log First
nodes.rationale: Every epistemic mutation is a signed contribution appended through Ledger::Append; projections are written only by Ledger::Apply.

nodes.label: Invariant 11 — Untrusted Text Stays Inert
nodes.rationale: Contributor notes and excerpts never reach scoring, and notes never reach another agent's packet; the server never fetches agent-supplied URLs.

nodes.label: Invariant 18 — Galedra Runs No Model
nodes.rationale: The only Llm::Adapter is the deterministic stub; a function needing a model becomes a task or a tool for a connected assistant whose answer is a signed contribution open to audit.

nodes.label: Order of Work — Log First, UI Last
nodes.norm_label: order of work — log first, ui last
nodes.rationale: Phases 0–7 build the signed log, projections and scoring before any UI, because the v2 roadmap built CRUD tables first and contradicted the handoff; tests follow the same order (security, log and scoring before UI).

nodes.label: Service Objects, Not Callbacks
nodes.rationale: Epistemic logic in Active Record callbacks is not explicit, testable, replayable or extractable; an append plus an apply plus a recompute job is.

nodes.label: Article XIV — Humans and AI Are Contributors, Not Oracles
nodes.norm_label: article xiv — humans and ai are contributors, not oracles
nodes.rationale: No model family should become a privileged source of truth; humans and AI are both subject to provenance, audit, evidence requirements and correction.

nodes.label: P-5 — The Ledger Runs No Model
nodes.norm_label: p-5 — the ledger runs no model
nodes.rationale: A model running inside the ledger would be an unattributed, unreproducible contributor whose outputs could not be replayed, audited or challenged. Keeping every model outside, behind a signed contribution, is what makes 'reproducible from the log' true.

nodes.label: The Hash Chain Was Unimplementable (v2 defect)
nodes.norm_label: the hash chain was unimplementable (v2 defect)
nodes.rationale: parent_hash inside the client signature cannot be known by an asynchronous agent, so the server now builds the chain around the client envelope under an advisory lock.

nodes.label: Prompt Injection Answered with Closed-Enum Ops
nodes.norm_label: prompt injection answered with closed-enum ops
nodes.rationale: 'Tell agents to ignore instructions' is not something the server can enforce; notes are excluded from packets, scoring and summary inputs instead.

nodes.label: Snapshots Could Not Be Reproduced (v2 defect)
nodes.norm_label: snapshots could not be reproduced (v2 defect)
nodes.rationale: Mutable status columns and timestamp-keyed snapshots made it impossible to know what was active at an earlier point; fixed by log-first event sourcing, gap-free seq, validity windows and a mandatory replay test.

nodes.label: No Server Fetch of Agent-Supplied URLs in P0
nodes.norm_label: no server fetch of agent-supplied urls in p0
nodes.rationale: 'Claimed source location accessible' implied fetching agent URLs, which is SSRF.

nodes.label: SUPERSEDE_LINK Added
nodes.rationale: The qualifier story requires revising another contributor's links, and the mechanism requires acceptance by a different principal.

nodes.label: Never fetch on an assistant's request (SSRF and untrusted input)
nodes.norm_label: never fetch on an assistant's request (ssrf and untrusted input)
nodes.rationale: An assistant's write must not make Galedra act on untrusted input: a URL in a bundle could point into the network behind the tunnel, at something enormous, or at a page that differs per visitor. Hosts are resolved before connecting and private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, multicast, reserved and IPv6-local addresses refused, re-checked on every redirect.

nodes.label: Finding 1 — ledger:replay Had Been Broken Since Stage 25 (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 1 — ledger:replay had been broken since stage 25 (fixed)
nodes.rationale: Tasks::Status was defined inside tasks/lease.rb, so Zeitwerk only resolved it once something had referenced Tasks::Lease. A web request always had; a rake task had not. Invariant 2 had not been checkable for several stages and it went unnoticed because the command is only run deliberately.

nodes.label: Finding 12 — A Refusal Was Logged Without Saying What Was Refused (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 12 — a refusal was logged without saying what was refused (fixed)
nodes.rationale: The assistant was told which field was wrong and the operator watching was not. An observability fix that pays for itself on its first occurrence is the cheapest kind there is.

nodes.label: Finding 13 — The Timestamp Format Was Not Where an Assistant Reads It (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 13 — the timestamp format was not where an assistant reads it (fixed)
nodes.rationale: 'RFC 3339' with no example invites a wrong guess, and the work topic never touched formats; the rule now sits in STANDING, which every topic carries.

nodes.label: Finding 14 — A Merged Claim's Checks Were Leased Forever (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 14 — a merged claim's checks were leased forever (fixed)
nodes.rationale: A livelock: the appliers refuse the task, releasing returns it to the head of the queue, and it blocked every filter that reached it. Cancelled rather than reassigned, because MERGE_CLAIMS is reversible.

nodes.label: Finding 15 — The Expired Lease Was Not a Bug; the Message Was (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 15 — the expired lease was not a bug; the message was (fixed)
nodes.rationale: An assistant has no reliable sense of wall time, so a correct expiry read as a future instant and became a bug report. A confident clock-skew hypothesis was measured and wrong.

nodes.label: Finding 16 — excerpt: "packet" Resolved to Nothing (FIXED)
nodes.rationale: QUALIFIER_CHECK carries no passage, so the schema promised what only one task type can deliver and validation failed downstream with a misleading 'expected a UUID'.

nodes.label: Finding 17 — Replay Works (VERIFIED)
nodes.rationale: 3,964 contributions re-applied; the autoload fix proven against real data, which the suite structurally could not do because no spec boots a cold rake task.

nodes.label: Finding 18 — Replay's First Run Found Rows Deleted Outside the Log (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 18 — replay's first run found rows deleted outside the log (fixed)
nodes.rationale: A second outline root with invalidated_seq nil on every section had been removed straight from the projections, which Invariant 2 forbids. Replay was right and the database was wrong; the remedy went through the log as a signed INVALIDATE by the outline's own principal.

nodes.label: Finding 19 — And Then It Held (VERIFIED)
nodes.rationale: A second replay over the withdrawal produced a byte-identical digest: the first demonstration in this project that Invariant 2 holds.

nodes.label: Finding 3 — The Write Cap Could Not Carry One Investigation (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 3 — the write cap could not carry one investigation (fixed)
nodes.rationale: 34 signed writes per leaf, about 1,600 for one transcript, against a named cap of 1,000 a day.

nodes.label: Finding 4 — server/discover Is Re-Probed Every Turn (OPEN)
nodes.norm_label: finding 4 — server/discover is re-probed every turn (open)
nodes.rationale: Supported versions, capabilities and identity cannot change without a restart, unlike tool descriptions, so ttlMs 0 is the wrong pairing for discover.

nodes.label: Finding 6 — Sections::Tree Counted Only What It Rendered (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 6 — sections::tree counted only what it rendered (fixed)
nodes.rationale: depth truncated what was counted, not just what was rendered, so any outline three levels deep would under-count silently at the default. Found by the assistant using the product, not by monitoring the data.

nodes.label: Finding 8 — Shipping a Behaviour Change Without Its Instructions (FIXED, third occurrence)
nodes.norm_label: finding 8 — shipping a behaviour change without its instructions (fixed, third occurrence)
nodes.rationale: Three times the code was right and the thing an assistant reads was wrong, and each time the tests passed, because nothing tests that an instruction matches the behaviour it describes.

nodes.label: Finding 9 — The Self-Check Counter Could Not See the Most Common Check (FIXED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 9 — the self-check counter could not see the most common check (fixed)
nodes.rationale: EVIDENCE_VERIFICATION is not a checklist item, so the most numerous check type was invisible to the figures built to report it. A spec that only tests the case you were thinking about confirms the case you were thinking about.

nodes.label: P0 Definition of Done
nodes.rationale: Twelve capabilities ending in the hardest one: drop all projection tables, replay the log, and get the same snapshot hashes and scores.

nodes.label: Experiment — A Connected Assistant Outlines a Two-Hour Transcript
nodes.norm_label: experiment — a connected assistant outlines a two-hour transcript
nodes.rationale: Tests whether the corrected size rule and wire-served guidance push the assistant onto the outline path; every number taken from the database rather than the assistant's account of itself.

nodes.label: Experiments Log Convention
nodes.rationale: An experiment is not a test and not a profiling run: it asks whether a person and an assistant, given the real thing, end up with what the design intended. A claim about how Galedra behaves with real input is worth what the run behind it is worth.

nodes.label: Invariant 2 — Replayable
nodes.rationale: Truncating projections and replaying the log reproduces identical projections and snapshot digests.

nodes.label: Article XX — Models May Change; Evidence Must Endure
nodes.norm_label: article xx — models may change; evidence must endure
nodes.rationale: The durable asset is the evidence graph and its provenance; the repository should become more valuable as reasoning models improve.

nodes.label: Near-Term Federation Readiness Properties
nodes.rationale: Durable IDs, append-only signed records, explicit schema versions, canonical serialization, replayable projections and explicit rights metadata are useful even if federation never occurs.

nodes.label: The Per-Delegate Limit Becomes Hourly
nodes.rationale: A measured 1,600 signed writes for one two-hour transcript stopped an investigation two thirds through under a 1,000-a-day cap; the cap exists to bound a runaway agent, not to make a legitimate long job impossible. Rolling rather than calendar, because a fixed boundary permits two caps a minute apart.

nodes.label: What Was Wrong in the Watching
nodes.norm_label: what was wrong in the watching
nodes.rationale: An observer who misreads the run is part of what the run revealed: sampling mid-write, calling a flake attributable on four data points, guessing schema names, reporting the data instead of the product, and repeating a mistake already written down.

nodes.label: Stage 21 — Large requests from a connector (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 21 — large requests from a connector (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Every piece already existed — the outline is Stage 20, the per-leaf CLAIM_EXTRACTION is P0, the volunteer answers through Stage 18, the proposal-only rule of 04 §4.3 and Stage 19's accept_proposal are the review step. This stage carries them over the connector in the order an assistant needs and adds the one judgment the server cannot make: the size rule.

nodes.label: The paste page as a third door
nodes.norm_label: the paste page as a third door
nodes.rationale: Hosted assistants differ in what they can reach - Claude.ai takes an MCP URL, ChatGPT Plus takes Actions but not a custom MCP server, a browsing-only session can call nothing - so anyone may paste the bundle an assistant drafted, and it records through the same service with a browser-session token minted on first use, so pasted work is signed, delegated, capped, sampled and attributed like an assistant's.

nodes.label: Duplicate check first
nodes.rationale: With a trigram candidate at similarity 0.6 or more and no on_duplicate: create, the call returns 409 with the candidates and nothing is appended, so the assistant resubmits with attach_to and its evidence lands on the existing claim instead of a twin; Invariant 15 still holds because only an accepted MERGE_CLAIMS merges anything.

nodes.label: One bundle with local handles, all or nothing
nodes.norm_label: one bundle with local handles, all or nothing
nodes.rationale: No id threading and no vocabulary beyond the enums: the bundle is validated structurally first, then appended in dependency order inside one transaction so any applier rejection rolls back every entry, and the response returns handle-to-id maps, a card per claim and each claim's URL.

nodes.label: plain.say_instead is rule-based and may be null
nodes.norm_label: plain.say_instead is rule-based and may be null
nodes.rationale: say_instead is null unless the graph supports a sentence - a narrower claim that holds up via NARROWS/BROADENS, else the strongest counted contradiction, else a counted qualifier - so nothing is invented (Invariant 10), and headlines stay fixed neutral phrases per state.

nodes.label: Sources recorded by link and hash
nodes.norm_label: sources recorded by link and hash
nodes.rationale: Outside a task CREATE_SOURCE accepts canonical_uri, content_hash and retrieved_at with no content, and the excerpt lives on a QUOTE or TRANSCRIPTION location; the log therefore records the link, the hash of what was read and the quoted passage, never a page's text (01 SS7), and replay reproduces it like any other source.

nodes.label: Say-instead line, short and plain
nodes.rationale: A supported claim is itself what to say, so a say-instead line is offered only when the claim as stated does not hold up; a candidate over 25 words is skipped rather than cut short, so the line is a whole graph sentence or absent. Nothing is composed or paraphrased (Invariant 10).

nodes.label: Daily cap 1,000 for named assistants, 200 for anonymous
nodes.norm_label: daily cap 1,000 for named assistants, 200 for anonymous
nodes.rationale: An outline plus its claims is far more writes than a meme check, and a named assistant has a principal someone can hold to account; the cap message names the outline so the assistant can say how far it got and that the rest is open work.

nodes.label: A section check — record_investigation with `section` per claim
nodes.norm_label: a section check — record_investigation with `section` per claim
nodes.rationale: When every claim sits under one root the reply's share line is the outline's counts line rather than a verdict, and the leaf's open CLAIM_EXTRACTION task is set CANCELLED with RECORDED_BY_REQUESTER — the task is not a log entry, so cancelling it is not a correction.

nodes.label: "Show me why"
nodes.rationale: Deterministically selected: strongest counted support and contradiction, suppressed dependents, review-coverage gaps, and the single evidence addition that would move the score most.

nodes.label: claim_edges
nodes.rationale: Stored and displayed and used for downstream_count, but edges do not propagate probability in v0.1 because propagation needs cycle handling and a real model.

nodes.label: summaries
nodes.rationale: A summary is stale when a newer snapshot changes its input_hash; no mutable stale flag.

nodes.label: review_coverage
nodes.rationale: Fraction of the review checklist completed.

nodes.label: stability
nodes.rationale: Sensitivity to model variants.

nodes.label: High-Impact Policy (P0 placeholder)
nodes.rationale: Confirming audits required before provisional clears scale with downstream_count; thresholds are placeholders and live in config.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/claims/:id/summary
nodes.rationale: The prose rendering of /why; replaces the previous draft's overlapping /explanation?length= route.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/claims/:id/why
nodes.rationale: Deterministic 'show me why' bundle; the structured data behind /summary.

nodes.label: Main unresolved issue
nodes.rationale: Chosen deterministically, first match wins: an invalidated or disputed audit; independence_unreviewed > 0; a QUALIFY link; contested; the first unmet review check; otherwise 'none recorded'.

nodes.label: Per-source answer card
nodes.rationale: One line per extracted claim plus a one-sentence roll-up; the P0 form of 'the graph powers answers'.

nodes.label: Task board
nodes.rationale: 'Hand this to my agent' copies a lease command for the example client; no in-browser agent in P0.

nodes.label: Scenario E - Fabricated citation
nodes.rationale: C4 leans contradicted and the per-source card flags the citation as unverified.

nodes.label: Scenario F - Coverage vs. probability
nodes.rationale: A claim is SUPPORTED with 1 of 4 review checks; the UI renders display rule 5.

nodes.label: Review coverage checklist
nodes.rationale: v3 defined coverage as reviewed/estimated evidence surface, a quantity nobody can estimate; v4 replaces it with a checklist derived entirely from the log, and the denominator comes from the model so no tier can cap coverage below 1.0.

nodes.label: Stability variants (conservative / permissive)
nodes.rationale: Spread between the default, x0.7 and x1.3 magnitudes; capped at MEDIUM below 2 independent groups and at LOW for INTERPRETIVE or CAUSAL, because weak evidence near 0.5 produces a small spread that would otherwise read as highly stable.

nodes.label: Task Priority Heuristic
nodes.rationale: uncertainty x impact x (0.5 + coverage_gap) / task_type_cost, used for the task board and never for scores; a heuristic, not expected information gain, and labeled as such.

nodes.label: What v0.1 Deliberately Does Not Do
nodes.norm_label: what v0.1 deliberately does not do
nodes.rationale: No claim-to-claim propagation, no diminishing-returns aggregation, no contributor-reliability weighting, no forecast dual scoring, no causal-identification metadata. Each is a candidate for a later model version, not a patch to v0.1.

nodes.label: Summaries (server-side P0 stub, stub-v0.1)
nodes.rationale: Summaries are derived caches, never evidence. Every sentence must have at least one cite drawn from the input set, or the summary is rejected and falls back to the stub; an LLM generator must pass the same validator.

nodes.label: Answer card
nodes.rationale: The default claim view. Users read 0.73 as '73% true' no matter how it is labeled, so the probability, trace and graph live behind Show calculation and Why?, and the number is available but never the headline.

nodes.label: Work done per contributor and the contributors list
nodes.norm_label: work done per contributor and the contributors list

nodes.label: Work counts derived, with the prestige tension recorded
nodes.norm_label: work counts derived, with the prestige tension recorded
nodes.rationale: Contributors::Tally derives everything from what exists with no new table, crediting an agent's entry to the principal of its delegation and leaving out invalidated entries and the system key. 06 SS5 says the contributor page shows no aggregate prestige and 14 SS20 warns against equating volume with quality, so the list ships as counts of work with a fixed sentence that they measure neither reliability nor authority, and it is not a scoring input.

nodes.label: Stage 9 - Why, summaries, answer cards, and weaknesses
nodes.norm_label: stage 9 - why, summaries, answer cards, and weaknesses

nodes.label: Atomicity is a warning, never a block
nodes.norm_label: atomicity is a warning, never a block
nodes.rationale: 02 SS4 asks for a heuristic, not a gate: length over 25 words, a conjunction joining clauses, a comma-separated series and inference words produce warnings returned with the POST response and on claim reads, leaving the contributor to decide.

nodes.label: Summaries only restate supplied graph content
nodes.norm_label: summaries only restate supplied graph content
nodes.rationale: Summaries::Input is the deterministic input and its cite set is the only thing a sentence may cite; the validator rejects any sentence without a cite or with a cite outside the set and the stub is served instead, which is the rule a real adapter would also have to pass.

nodes.label: Headlines in neutral words
nodes.rationale: 06 SS4 rule 12 forbids true, false, debunked and confirmed, so state is rendered as fixed neutral phrases and the number stays in the assessment block, never in the headline.

nodes.label: claim_scores
nodes.rationale: Cache only - delete freely.

nodes.label: graph_snapshots
nodes.rationale: A snapshot is just a pinned (seq, entry_hash); Merkle trees are unnecessary because the chain head commits to the whole prefix.

nodes.label: contested
nodes.rationale: Both support and contradiction groups > 0; an orthogonal flag, not a lifecycle state.

nodes.label: independence_unreviewed
nodes.rationale: Counted items with no independence group.

nodes.label: ledger-default@0.1.0
nodes.rationale: The display default, labeled as a default and not as 'the' answer (Art. XIX).

nodes.label: ledger-strict@0.1.0
nodes.rationale: Same §4 code, different config: scores only directly observable types (drops INTERPRETIVE and CAUSAL) and gives EXPERT_ANALYSIS weight 0.0.

nodes.label: model_dependent
nodes.rationale: Claim type is in config.model_dependent_types.

nodes.label: not_applicable_reason
nodes.rationale: Why no assessment was made (constitution Art. VI).

nodes.label: Priors (v0.1)
nodes.rationale: All scored types use p0 = 0.50 except CAUSAL = 0.35, a nudge against treating correlation as causation. These values aim at reproducibility, not calibration.

nodes.label: probability
nodes.rationale: Null unless the state is a scored state; never displayed without model version and snapshot.

nodes.label: Score Trace
nodes.rationale: Canonical JSON hashed into trace_hash; all decimals are strings with fixed places.

nodes.label: Step 0 - Applicability
nodes.rationale: If truth_evaluable is false or the type is not in scored_types, return NOT_APPLICABLE with no probability; review_coverage is still computed.

nodes.label: Step 4 - Combine
nodes.rationale: posterior = prior_log_odds + evidence_sum summed in ascending link.id order; probability = sigmoid rounded to 4 places.

nodes.label: Step 5 - Assessment state
nodes.rationale: First match wins over config.state_thresholds; contested and provisional are orthogonal flags displayed alongside the state.

nodes.label: trace
nodes.rationale: Everything needed to recompute the result by hand.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/claims/:id/compare
nodes.rationale: Returns both traces plus a diff naming the links whose effective weights differ, the config keys responsible, and any state change.

nodes.label: Weaknesses page
nodes.rationale: Art. XXII: deterministic lists of under-reviewed, provisional, independence-unreviewed, contested and model-disagreeing claims, each with the 'what would most change this' item.

nodes.label: Scenario H - Alternative model
nodes.rationale: C6 is UNRESOLVED under ledger-default and NOT_APPLICABLE (NOT_SCORED_BY_MODEL) under ledger-strict; /compare names scored_types as responsible.

nodes.label: What determinism is promised (narrowed in v4)
nodes.norm_label: what determinism is promised (narrowed in v4)
nodes.rationale: Same implementation, seq and model gives a byte-identical canonical trace; different implementations must match on the golden fixtures and shared regression corpus only.

nodes.label: Directional states require matching evidence
nodes.rationale: v4 fix: with a non-0.50 prior the v3 rule could label a claim leans-contradicted when every counted link supported it (demo C6: prior 0.35 plus weak support = 0.3792). The prior alone can never produce a directional state.

nodes.label: Multiple Models (P0)
nodes.rationale: Constitution Article XII requires alternative scoring models over the same evidence; /compare localizes the disagreement (Art. XVI). Adding a model must never change another model's results.

nodes.label: Warning About Probability
nodes.rationale: Say '0.86 under ledger-default@0.1.0 at snapshot 212', never 'this claim is 86% true'; priors and weights in v0.1 are hand-set and uncalibrated.

nodes.label: rounding_boundary
nodes.rationale: The spec does not claim exp/ln are bit-identical across libm builds; a value within config.rounding.boundary_guard (1e-6) of a rounding boundary is flagged so cross-implementation comparisons treat it as needing review rather than as a failure.

nodes.label: Deterministic audit sampling
nodes.rationale: The decision is sha256(entry_hash + policy_version) < audit_probability * 2^256, so anyone can recompute whether a contribution should have been sampled and operators cannot quietly skip audits.

nodes.label: Scoring Model Releases
nodes.rationale: Weights never change without a new version and old versions stay loadable so old traces reproduce; a release is rejected if its review_checklist declares a check no available task type can satisfy.

nodes.label: claim_score_digest
nodes.rationale: sha256 over the sorted (claim_id, trace_hash) list at a seq under the default model; two installations with the same log must return the same digest.

nodes.label: Display Rules (normative)
nodes.rationale: Lead with the compact answer, never the graph or the number; no number at all for INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE or NOT_APPLICABLE; review coverage always as a count of checks; no persuasive framing, colour-coding, debunked/confirmed badges or ranking of claims by wrongness.

nodes.label: Model selector
nodes.rationale: Always available next to the assessment; the default model is labeled as a default, not as 'the' answer (Art. XIX).

nodes.label: Personal views, affiliations, and content review
nodes.norm_label: personal views, affiliations, and content review

nodes.label: Affiliation breakdown hidden below MIN_GROUP
nodes.rationale: An affiliation is shown only when at least five people holding it registered a view on that claim, so a small group can never expose anyone; special-category data is self-declared, optional and deletable, and the table says how groups split, never which group is right (Article XVIII).

nodes.label: Affiliation requests resolved by rules, escalated to consensus
nodes.norm_label: affiliation requests resolved by rules, escalated to consensus
nodes.rationale: The LLM boundary maps a request to EXACT, ALIAS, SIMILAR or NONE; EXACT and ALIAS are applied at once by a job while SIMILAR and NONE go to consensus review, and the agreed verdict settles every pending request for the same normalized text together. A real adapter must return the same shape and is never trusted beyond EXACT and ALIAS without a person.

nodes.label: Consensus, not admins
nodes.rationale: There are no paid admins, so review is settled by agreement: one verdict per principal per item, the author never votes on their own text (the 04 SS3.1 distinct-principals rule and Article XI's no self-certification), two agreeing verdicts settle at once, and a single uncontradicted verdict settles after 48 hours so a quiet queue drains with one honest reviewer. No leases, because several principals judging the same item is the point.

nodes.label: Off-log free text is reviewed off the log
nodes.norm_label: off-log free text is reviewed off the log
nodes.rationale: Every non-empty free-text field written outside the log is queued for review; log content is not queued because it has quarantine and takedown. It is deliberately not a ledger task type: 04 SS2 task types target claims and sources and their results are signed ops, so reviewing bug reports through the log would put moderation of bug reports into the epistemic record. OFFENSIVE replaces the field with a redaction marker and keeps the original for admins.

nodes.label: Personal views stay outside the log
nodes.norm_label: personal views stay outside the log
nodes.rationale: personal_assessments is never fed to Ledger::Apply, scoring, packets or summaries; the claim page shows the person's own view and the aggregate below the assessment, both carrying the fixed sentence that views are personal belief, not evidence, and visibility stays PRIVATE so a stance is never shown with a name.

nodes.label: Stage 4 - Quarantine, takedown, and the moderation log
nodes.norm_label: stage 4 - quarantine, takedown, and the moderation log

nodes.label: Moderators designated outside the log
nodes.rationale: 09 SS15 leaves appointment open and inventing an APPOINT_MODERATOR action would extend the closed list in 02 SS3.6, so moderators are key ids in LEDGER_MODERATOR_KEY_IDS or a users.moderator flag; the list is published by /api/v1/meta and /api/v1/moderation so the power is at least visible, and the system key is never a moderator.

nodes.label: Quarantine leaves a public stub
nodes.rationale: Nothing disappears without a public trace: a quarantined claim keeps its URL and returns a stub with the quarantine seq, moderator key id, reason from the closed list and the appeal path, while text and qualifiers are withheld from every public read including old snapshots, because the point is not to serve the text.

nodes.label: TAKEDOWN carries a signed redaction manifest
nodes.norm_label: takedown carries a signed redaction manifest
nodes.rationale: A legally compelled deletion must still verify, so the manifest names for every projection row the fields removed and the retained values, is validated against the current rows, and leaves payload_hash, envelope_hash, entry_hash and server_signature intact; verify then reports CHAIN_VERIFIED_WITH_REDACTIONS and breaks on bytes removed any other way, and replay rebuilds the rows from the manifest.

nodes.label: Moderator appointment by an admin (a visible stopgap)
nodes.norm_label: moderator appointment by an admin (a visible stopgap)
nodes.rationale: The reserved decision — who holds the system key and appoints moderators — still stands. The appointment is visible (meta lists every moderator key) but not in the log; when the owner decides, a signed APPOINT_MODERATOR control entry can replace the flag, and Governance::Moderators is the one reader.

nodes.label: Append-only database role galedra_app
nodes.rationale: Grants are not in schema.rb, so Ledger::DatabaseRole.ensure_all! re-applies them after every db task and schema load: everything granted, then UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE revoked on contributions with UPDATE (current_status) granted back; runtime connections SET ROLE, and as_owner is the explicit escape hatch used by takedown and by tests that corrupt rows.

nodes.label: Block-scoped connections for concurrent appends
nodes.rationale: Rails 7.2+ leases a connection to the thread for good when code calls Model.connection, so the first Append starved a 50-thread test after five appends; services now use with_connection and fifty concurrent appends complete in about 0.2 s.

nodes.label: Custody material moved off contributors
nodes.rationale: 02 SS3.1 puts encrypted_private_key and user_id on contributors, but replay truncates projections and the log cannot rebuild key material, so custody lives in custodied_keys, which is not a projection and survives replay; no foreign keys point at projection tables so a single TRUNCATE still works.

nodes.label: Deterministic projection ids
nodes.rationale: Replay must reproduce projection rows byte for byte (02 SS1.1 rule 3), which UUIDv7 cannot do, so log rows keep UUIDv7 while projection rows get Ledger::Ids.derive(contribution_id, kind), a UUID with version nibble 8 derived from sha256; projection tables also carry no timestamps because created_seq is the time axis.

nodes.label: Hash chain and entry_hash
nodes.rationale: entry_hash = sha256(canonical({seq, prev_hash, envelope_hash, received_at})) per 02 SS1.2; genesis prev_hash is 64 zeros with no prefix and received_at is floored to microseconds before hashing so the stored timestamptz round-trips and the chain still recomputes.

nodes.label: Idempotency key over signer, task, and payload hash
nodes.norm_label: idempotency key over signer, task, and payload hash
