nodes.rationale: idempotency_key = sha256(signer_key_id|task_id|payload_hash) per 02 SS3.1, and the duplicate check runs before any other validation so a resubmission always returns the original even for a REGISTER_KEY whose key is by then registered; the consequence is that a byte-identical payload can never make a second distinct claim.

nodes.label: RETRIEVE_SOURCE control contribution
nodes.rationale: System-signed, takes effect on append, projecting to source_retrievals in PROJECTION_MODELS so digests, replay, verify and TAKEDOWN redaction cover it. Page text is never stored: only the hash, the size and one finding per quoted location (VERBATIM, NORMALIZED, NOT_FOUND, UNSUPPORTED). The source keeps the reader's own content_hash; the server's hash is shown alongside, never overwriting it.

nodes.label: CREATE_SECTION — one contribution creates one subtree
nodes.norm_label: create_section — one contribution creates one subtree
nodes.rationale: An assistant records an outline of a few hundred sections in one signed write: nested at most 6 levels, 500 nodes per contribution, 2,000 per root, 120-character headings, and a 300-character quoted anchor that locates the place rather than reproducing the passage. Headings are untrusted display text, never scored. Ids derive from the contribution in preorder.

nodes.label: task_assignments
nodes.rationale: Unique per (task, principal) so one principal cannot fill every independent slot with its own agents.

nodes.label: extraction_factor
nodes.rationale: UNVERIFIED factors are 1.0 on purpose: the provisional flag, not a hidden discount, communicates that work is unaudited.

nodes.label: observation_weight
nodes.rationale: MODEL_OUTPUT is 0.0: an AI assertion never counts as evidence on its own.

nodes.label: Step 2 - Weight each link
nodes.rationale: magnitude = relevance x observation x interpretation x authenticity x extraction, round half-even at 6 places; a missing config key is a release-time validation error, never a runtime default.

nodes.label: Step 3 - Independence (strongest-only)
nodes.rationale: Within each (group_key, sign) pair keep only the largest magnitude, ties broken deterministically; grouping is per direction so a group can contribute one support and one contradiction weight.

nodes.label: Scenario C - Dependent evidence
nodes.rationale: Three articles and a press release repeat one survey: four lineages SUPPORTED 0.9085 becomes one lineage LEANS_SUPPORTED 0.7146 after the independence check.

nodes.label: Blind independent verification
nodes.rationale: Each assignee gets the same packet and no information about other assignees; results are revealed only after all slots submit or leases expire.

nodes.label: Independence of verification processes
nodes.rationale: Two agents with different keys but the same model, prompt family or retrieval path can repeat the same mistake. P0 enforces distinct principals per slot; P1 adds model-family and retrieval-path constraints, which raise the cost of correlated error but cannot eliminate it because declared model metadata is self-reported.

nodes.label: Sybil Resistance
nodes.rationale: Cryptographic identity alone does not stop one actor from creating 10,000 keys; nothing in scoring counts heads, slots are unique per principal, new identities are heavily audited and rate-limited, and evidence must be reproducible from stored bytes.

nodes.label: Correlated AI errors
nodes.rationale: The same model, prompt or retrieval path making the same mistake under different keys; mitigated partially by distinct principals per slot and recorded software metadata, which is unverifiable.

nodes.label: Threat Model
nodes.rationale: Eighteen adversarial threats each paired with a P0 mitigation. The POC does not claim to solve selective omission, agent collusion, correlated AI errors or low-quality donated agents; it must avoid the naive 'more validators = more truth' model.

nodes.label: Claim Identity Test — C2 and C3 Must Not Merge
nodes.norm_label: claim identity test — c2 and c3 must not merge
nodes.rationale: Two claims differing by a few words trigger the trigram duplicate suggestion but need different evidence and end with different assessments; the correct relationship is the explicit edge C3 NARROWS C2.

nodes.label: Independence Collapse — Four Sources, One Origin (G1)
nodes.norm_label: independence collapse — four sources, one origin (g1)
nodes.rationale: A press release and three news articles repeating one Acme survey are grouped SAME_DATASET, so the probability falls from 0.9085 to 0.7146 when the repetition is recognised as repetition.

nodes.label: Replay Check — Truncate, Replay, Compare Digests
nodes.norm_label: replay check — truncate, replay, compare digests

nodes.label: Competing Hypotheses H1–H3 (P1)
nodes.rationale: No hypothesis is marked as the answer; the question page shows them side by side.

nodes.label: Double Counting and Its Correction (C1 S4→S5)
nodes.norm_label: double counting and its correction (c1 s4→s5)
nodes.rationale: The demo's key teaching moment: the probability goes down, 0.9683 to 0.9468, when an analyst discovers that two sources are one.

nodes.label: Example Task Packets and Deterministic Stub Agents
nodes.norm_label: example task packets and deterministic stub agents
nodes.rationale: Stub agents read fixed answers from fixtures.json rather than matching keywords, because a heuristic stub would be flaky and would teach nothing.

nodes.label: Finding 20 — Verifying a Transcript Was Corroborating the Claim (OPEN, most serious)
nodes.norm_label: finding 20 — verifying a transcript was corroborating the claim (open, most serious)
nodes.rationale: 24 of 29 directionally supported claims rested on the episode agreeing with itself, and duplicate Source rows for one URI make same-origin evidence look independent. Not a quick fix, because scoring is versioned: changing how support is weighed requires a new model version, new goldens and a reference-scorer pass.

nodes.label: Golden Values (both models, checkpoints S1–S5)
nodes.rationale: Exact expected probabilities, states, coverage and group counts under ledger-default@0.1.0 and ledger-strict@0.1.0, so byte-identical reproduction has something to test against. A golden value is never edited to make an implementation pass.

nodes.label: Public Demo — AI-Drafted Memo with a Viral Statistic
nodes.norm_label: public demo — ai-drafted memo with a viral statistic
nodes.rationale: Chosen as the first public demonstration because it shows the ledger doing something ordinary and useful — checking an AI-drafted paragraph — rather than appearing fringe-adjacent, which the Watchers example risked.

nodes.label: Watchers Stress Test (internal)
nodes.rationale: Kept because it exercises primary texts, interpretation, an unusual hypothesis, unsupported extrapolation and a model disagreement in a small space — but deliberately not the first thing outsiders see.

nodes.label: Automated Independence Inference
nodes.rationale: Agents propose independence clusters from citation graphs, timing and shared datasets; proposals remain auditable contributions rather than silent system judgments.

nodes.label: Invariant 15 — No Text-Uniqueness for Claims
nodes.rationale: Similarity proposes relationships; only an accepted, reversible MERGE_CLAIMS merges.

nodes.label: Invariant 6 — No Double Counting
nodes.rationale: Dependent evidence is suppressed per independence group and direction, visibly in the trace.

nodes.label: Article IV — Atomicity
nodes.rationale: Small independently evaluable claims enable precise correction, evidence reuse, dependency analysis, localized disagreement, and efficient agent contribution.

nodes.label: Article IX — Evidence Independence Matters
nodes.rationale: Ten dependent repetitions must not be treated as ten independent observations; repetition is not corroboration.

nodes.label: Claim Identity Is a Major Open Problem
nodes.norm_label: claim identity is a major open problem
nodes.rationale: Aggressive semantic deduplication destroys important distinctions and loose deduplication fragments evidence; semantic search should propose SAME_AS / NARROWS / BROADENS / QUALIFIES, and merging must be explicit, attributable, auditable and reversible.

nodes.label: Correlated AI Error
nodes.rationale: Two AI agents are not necessarily independent — shared model family, training biases, retrieval sources and common hallucinations — so verification independence should be modeled separately from source independence.

nodes.label: Recommended Public Demo — Citation Laundering, Missing Qualifier, AI Citation Hallucination
nodes.norm_label: recommended public demo — citation laundering, missing qualifier, ai citation hallucination
nodes.rationale: Demonstrates value without making the project appear fringe-adjacent, which the ancient-text example risked.

nodes.label: GNU Affero General Public License v3.0 or later
nodes.norm_label: gnu affero general public license v3.0 or later

nodes.label: Open Data Commons Open Database License 1.0
nodes.norm_label: open data commons open database license 1.0

nodes.label: Reference node software: AGPL-3.0-or-later
nodes.rationale: Galedra is primarily network software, so AGPL preserves source availability when a modified node is operated as a service rather than distributed; this aligns with the constitutional preference for inspectable machinery over trusted authority.

nodes.label: Protocol, schemas, test vectors and SDKs: Apache-2.0
nodes.norm_label: protocol, schemas, test vectors and sdks: apache-2.0
nodes.rationale: The protocol must be easier to adopt than the reference server so the federation is larger than one implementation; Apache-2.0 also carries an explicit patent grant, useful for widely implemented infrastructure.

nodes.label: Individual project-authored factual records: CC0-1.0
nodes.rationale: Individual facts should be maximally reusable and the project should not attempt a copyright moat around facts; CC0 for contents plus ODbL for the collection keeps that distinction clean.

nodes.label: Project-authored prose and documentation: CC BY 4.0
nodes.norm_label: project-authored prose and documentation: cc by 4.0

nodes.label: Federation Charter, separate from copyright licences
nodes.norm_label: federation charter, separate from copyright licences
nodes.rationale: Copyright licences answer what you may legally do with the code and the database; required behavior for a recognized federation node is a governance question and belongs in a charter, not a licence.

nodes.label: Public federated database: ODbL-1.0
nodes.rationale: The project wants more than permission to copy the database: it wants public derivative databases to remain part of an open data commons, which ODbL's share-alike at the database layer preserves.

nodes.label: Imported third-party material stays under its original licence
nodes.norm_label: imported third-party material stays under its original licence

nodes.label: Determinism is not objectivity
nodes.rationale: Relevance labels, interpretive steps, independence groupings and claim wording are judgments; making them explicit, attributed, challengeable and versioned is honest, pretending they are objective is not.

nodes.label: contributors
nodes.rationale: No UNSIGNED tier: every contribution is signed, and identity_tier never affects scores.

nodes.label: Leases
nodes.rationale: Two-hour default; one active lease per (task, contributor) and per (task, principal); expired leases release the slot and a late submission is rejected at step 3. Delegations signed before max_tasks_per_hour was renamed carry max_tasks_per_day and the applier reads either, so replay reproduces them unchanged.

nodes.label: Server-Side Validation Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Nine ordered checks; failures return 422 with a machine-readable error list and create no contribution, because there is nothing to log and nothing signed by us.

nodes.label: SYSTEM custody (system key)
nodes.rationale: Lives outside the database in environment/credentials; its public key is published in GET /api/v1/meta.

nodes.label: GET /api/v1/meta
nodes.rationale: System key, current seq, model list, schema URLs, constitution_hash and version.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/contributions
nodes.rationale: The only write endpoint; task results are submitted here with action_type TASK_RESULT.

nodes.label: POST /api/v1/tasks/next
nodes.rationale: Leases one task, or 204.

nodes.label: Phase 0 - Skeleton
nodes.rationale: Constitution copied into the repo root with its hash exposed by /api/v1/meta; Rails 8.x, Docker Compose, Solid Queue, Active Storage, Hotwire, CI. Not pgvector, Redis, Sidekiq, a JS frontend or any external service.

nodes.label: No server-side fetching of agent-supplied URLs (SSRF)
nodes.norm_label: no server-side fetching of agent-supplied urls (ssrf)
nodes.rationale: New external sources are stored metadata-only with retrieval_pending, and a human or trusted job imports content later.

nodes.label: Keys and Custody (Ed25519)
nodes.rationale: Server custody for browser UI users is an honest, labeled compromise for a POC: the previous draft required signatures but gave UI users no way to sign. Never hand-roll primitives.

nodes.label: API Principles
nodes.rationale: REST/JSON, boring and inspectable. Reads are public except quarantined content; there is exactly one write path because resource-specific POST routes duplicated validation and invited a second write path that bypasses the log.

nodes.label: code_hash published beside config_hash
nodes.rationale: 03 SS1 says a probability is never shown without both, so Scoring::Registry hashes app/services/scoring/**/*.rb and RELEASE_SCORING_MODEL rejects a stale code_hash; golden tests compare output fields rather than trace hashes so a refactor changes code_hash without invalidating the goldens.

nodes.label: Golden fixture generated from the spec's reference scorer
nodes.norm_label: golden fixture generated from the spec's reference scorer
nodes.rationale: A generator imports reference_scorer.py and emits every row of 08 SS8 and Watchers SS7 for both models, so the Ruby scorer is checked against an independent implementation rather than against itself; fixture link ids are zero-padded so string order equals the reference's integer order.

nodes.label: rounding_boundary applied to 4-place values only
nodes.rationale: At 6 places an absolute 1e-6 guard equals a whole unit and would flag every value, so the guard applies to the 4-place probability and its two variants; the 6-place prior log-odds is a per-type constant every implementation can pin. Recorded as an interpretation of 03 SS10.

nodes.label: The most-moving addition favours self-critique
nodes.rationale: Cards::Why re-runs the scorer with one hypothetical independent DIRECT MEASUREMENT link in each direction and breaks ties toward the contradicting addition, so the answer to what would most change this leans against the current state rather than confirming it.

nodes.label: ledger-default@0.2.0 and ledger-strict@0.2.0, with 0.1.0 unchanged
nodes.rationale: Invariant 4 requires a new version for a scorer change, so old numbers are not silently restated: a claim that read 0.83 under 0.1.0 still reads 0.83 under 0.1.0, and the change is visible as a model rather than applied as a correction. Forty trace hashes captured before and after were identical (digest 30b8f47c). LEDGER_DEFAULT_MODEL pins the default, because default_model returned the newest released model and ledger:release_models would otherwise have made the switch silently.

nodes.label: After P0 - Landing page and visual design
nodes.norm_label: after p0 - landing page and visual design

nodes.label: Stage 11 - Seeded demos and P0 Definition of Done
nodes.norm_label: stage 11 - seeded demos and p0 definition of done

nodes.label: The landing animation is decorative and reads no ledger data
nodes.norm_label: the landing animation is decorative and reads no ledger data
nodes.rationale: A canvas graph grows behind the landing page purely as decoration: it reads no ledger data, pauses when the tab is hidden and shows one static frame under prefers-reduced-motion, and rule 12 still holds across the new stylesheet - no true/false colours and no badges of correctness.

nodes.label: P1 design rules for connected assistants
nodes.norm_label: p1 design rules for connected assistants
nodes.rationale: The target user is about to repost something and will not learn a vocabulary, so: one instruction and one link back; assistants cannot hold keys, so the server signs for them under a delegation naming the assistant; Galedra stores a link plus a content hash and never fetches URLs or stores a page's full text; anonymous contributions are weighted in sampling, priority, rate limits and labelling but never in scores, because identity does not replace evidence; and every result leads with a plain headline and a what-to-say-instead line before any number.

nodes.label: bin/demo refuses a log that already holds contributions
nodes.norm_label: bin/demo refuses a log that already holds contributions
nodes.rationale: 01 SS7's runs on a clean database is enforced rather than assumed: --reset truncates under the owner role, raises outside development and test, and unknown arguments abort with usage, so a typo cannot truncate a log or seed the wrong demo.

nodes.label: Seed tasks answered by the example agent in-process
nodes.norm_label: seed tasks answered by the example agent in-process
nodes.rationale: The fixture-driven client runs through Rack::MockRequest so the demo exercises the real lease, packet verification and result submission path rather than calling services directly; it found two real bugs, a canonicalizer turning false into null and a summary input ignoring audits on later-invalidated links.

nodes.label: 01 §7 — No page text in the log
nodes.norm_label: 01 §7 — no page text in the log

nodes.label: Compact Answer Cards
nodes.rationale: What most users see: a cited plain-language answer whose every clause names graph IDs, with the number available under Show calculation.

nodes.label: Finding 7 — Self-Certification Is Narrower Than It Reads (NO ACTION NEEDED)
nodes.norm_label: finding 7 — self-certification is narrower than it reads (no action needed)
nodes.rationale: Self-certification blocks task leasing and audits, not scoring; Tasks::Lease was stricter than the spec it implements, so the code was changed rather than the rule.

nodes.label: Stage 34 — Self-Performed Checks in the Wild
nodes.norm_label: stage 34 — self-performed checks in the wild
nodes.rationale: A person who pays to outline a two-hour source must be able to finish checking it rather than wait for a stranger who may never arrive; self-performed results are filtered before the scorer sees them, so they cannot move review_coverage and no new model version was needed.

nodes.label: Proofweave
nodes.rationale: Technically the closest example of the agent contribution model — delegated identity, signed envelopes, verification gates, append-only receipts — but its formal-mathematics verification guarantees do not generalize to empirical reasoning.

nodes.label: Stage 17 — Source retrieval by a trusted job (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 17 — source retrieval by a trusted job (implemented)
nodes.rationale: A source recorded by link is later checked by Galedra itself, under Galedra's own rules. The reader's record is never changed; the server's finding sits beside it. An assistant can never ask for the fetch and never steers it: the only input is a link already in the log.

nodes.label: Privacy-Preserving Identity
nodes.rationale: Improve Sybil resistance without requiring public real names.

nodes.label: Invariant 10 — Summaries Only Restate Supplied Graph Content
nodes.norm_label: invariant 10 — summaries only restate supplied graph content
nodes.rationale: Every sentence of a summary cites graph IDs.

nodes.label: Invariant 9 — No Self-Certification
nodes.rationale: No certification by the same contributor or the same principal.

nodes.label: Article II — Evidence Must Be Traceable
nodes.norm_label: article ii — evidence must be traceable
nodes.rationale: A conclusion that cannot be traced downward to evidence or explicit assumptions must be visibly distinguished from one that can.

nodes.label: Article XI — Identity Does Not Replace Evidence
nodes.norm_label: article xi — identity does not replace evidence
nodes.rationale: Cryptographic identity creates accountability and auditability, not hierarchy; a signature proves who submitted and that nothing was altered, not that it is correct.

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q1 — Does it make evidence more traceable or less?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q1 — does it make evidence more traceable or less?

nodes.label: P-1 — Protection of Persons
nodes.rationale: A permanent, signed, append-only ledger of scored assertions is an unusually durable defamation and doxxing vector; the constitution protects contributors' privacy but says nothing about the people claims are about. The safeguard against abusing the restriction power is that restriction is never silent.

nodes.label: Extraction Accepted by the System
nodes.rationale: Extraction was the only task type held as a proposal, so a volunteer's work sat unusable; accepting it makes the claims the extractor's principal's, which forced the demo's checks onto a second volunteer because a principal never checks its own claim.

nodes.label: Optional page hash for a source held by reference
nodes.norm_label: optional page hash for a source held by reference
nodes.rationale: Hosted assistants (claude.ai) see rendered text, not page bytes, so Claude rightly refused to invent a content_hash and recorded nothing. What Galedra verifies for such a source is the quoted excerpt with its own hash, the link and the time of reading; tools now say to omit the hash rather than fabricate it. Article II still holds.

nodes.label: Sources::Retrieve::Fetcher — a one-method seam so tests touch no network
nodes.norm_label: sources::retrieve::fetcher — a one-method seam so tests touch no network
nodes.rationale: The whole fetch is behind `get(uri)`, so specs use canned pages and a fake resolver. Five redirects, 2 MB streamed with an abort, 5 s open and 10 s read, a fixed user agent naming build and node, one fetch per host per minute through Rails.cache, robots.txt honoured with longest-match wins.

nodes.label: A retrieval finding is a label, not a scored review check
nodes.norm_label: a retrieval finding is a label, not a scored review check
nodes.rationale: Deviation from the plan's wording: review checks are part of the scored checklist and must not change (Article XI reading), so the confirmation is a label beside them, derived at read time. A NOT_FOUND excerpt adds a note to the claim's open EVIDENCE_VERIFICATION task rather than moving any score.

nodes.label: 02 §1.1a — Epistemic vs control actions, acceptance by a different principal
nodes.norm_label: 02 §1.1a — epistemic vs control actions, acceptance by a different principal

nodes.label: Stage 18 — Work open tasks from a connector (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 18 — work open tasks from a connector (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Task work is what the agent protocol was built for; this stage only carries it over the connector in a shape an assistant can use without learning refs, packet hashes or signing. The packet hash and lease expiry stay server-side.

nodes.label: Stage 19 — Correct what is recorded, from a connector (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 19 — correct what is recorded, from a connector (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Every primitive already existed in the log (SUPERSEDE_CLAIM, MERGE_CLAIMS, SUPERSEDE_LINK, ACCEPT, tasks); none was reachable from a connector and the website had no way to accept a proposal, so a correction proposed by anyone but the claim's own principal waited forever. Nothing is deleted; invalidation stays with human audits.

nodes.label: TAG_CLAIM epistemic contribution
nodes.rationale: Filing is a judgment, so it is a signed contribution projected to `claim_topics` with validity windows: auto-accepted only for the claim's own principal, PENDING as a proposal on someone else's claim, superseded deterministically at apply time by a later tag from the same principal. Unknown paths are TOPIC_UNKNOWN; a delegation may restrict `permissions.topics`.

nodes.label: Audits stay human (no audit tool for assistants)
nodes.norm_label: audits stay human (no audit tool for assistants)
nodes.rationale: 05 §8 admits as auditor a human at ESTABLISHED+ or a contributor with a track record in AUDIT; an assistant under a delegation is neither, so an audit tool would be refused for everyone who could reach it. Whether an agent acting for an ESTABLISHED+ human may audit is a constitutional-scope question reserved for the owner, not a code change.

nodes.label: Partial unique indexes on task_assignments (one ACTIVE lease)
nodes.norm_label: partial unique indexes on task_assignments (one active lease)
nodes.rationale: The unique indexes were unconditional, so a contributor whose lease expired could never take the task again and the retry-on-conflict loop spun until Postgres ran out of lock memory. They are now partial on LEASED and SUBMITTED, matching 04 §7's "one active lease", with a bounded retry and every lookup taking the contributor's latest row.

nodes.label: Claims created in the same TASK_RESULT count as current
nodes.norm_label: claims created in the same task_result count as current
nodes.rationale: A claim created earlier in a result was rejected as unaccepted when a later op linked to it or drew an edge from it, which made the qualifier task's "narrower claim with an edge" impossible. Edges and links now treat same-result claims as current, and the result is accepted or held as one.

nodes.label: Connector acceptance scope, stricter than the applier's
nodes.norm_label: connector acceptance scope, stricter than the applier's
nodes.rationale: The applier admits any different principal; the connector and the claim page admit only the target's own principal, any named principal when the target's is anonymous, or a moderator. Declining is leaving a proposal pending — there is no REJECT — and proposals do not expire (both reserved).

nodes.label: Guidance in results, not in tool descriptions
nodes.norm_label: guidance in results, not in tool descriptions
nodes.rationale: Hosts cache the tool list from the moment of connection, so rule text in descriptions goes stale until a person reconnects, while results are read fresh on every call. Tool names and input schemas are treated as an interface: additive and batched, since only those need a reconnect. tools/list_changed is not sent: it needs a streaming channel Galedra does not serve and would not refresh a host's stored catalog anyway.

nodes.label: revise_claim, merge_claims, revise_link, open_task, list_proposals, accept_proposal
nodes.norm_label: revise_claim, merge_claims, revise_link, open_task, list_proposals, accept_proposal
nodes.rationale: Own work is fixed at once and someone else's becomes a proposal that says whose acceptance it waits for; an assistant must never claim something was fixed when it is a proposal. carry_links re-issues every counted link onto the corrected claim, signed by whoever affirms the new text — the reviser for own work, the acceptor for a proposal.

nodes.label: Validity badges on the check page (departure from 06 §4 rule 12)
nodes.norm_label: validity badges on the check page (departure from 06 §4 rule 12)
nodes.rationale: Rule 12 forbids colour-coding claims; the owner chose ten green-to-red SVG badges for the page people paste into social media, and they appear nowhere else — claim pages, cards and the API stay neutral. The labels keep evidence wording rather than "true" or "false", which Article XXII rules out. 06 §4 rule 12 should be revised by the owner to name this exception.

nodes.label: The whole statement rule and Investigations::Verdict
nodes.norm_label: the whole statement rule and investigations::verdict
nodes.rationale: A five-claim meme came back as a two-claim check page because the assistant recorded only the new claims. Every claim a statement makes now goes into one record call, existing ones by reference, opinions as NORMATIVE. The verdict is display composition read from the claims' states — never a percentage, never a change to a claim score.

nodes.label: The requester may accept its volunteers' extractions
nodes.norm_label: the requester may accept its volunteers' extractions
nodes.rationale: It is a different principal from the extractor, and accepting makes every accepted claim its principal's responsibility, which is also what lets its tasks on those claims be worked by others and not by itself. The applier still refuses the extractor's own principal.

nodes.label: blind_requested — splitting a deliberate blind hand-off from routine opening
nodes.norm_label: blind_requested — splitting a deliberate blind hand-off from routine opening
nodes.rationale: Stage 19's guard "whoever asks for a blind check does not perform it" keyed on created_by, which is set both when someone deliberately calls open_task and when verification opens routinely alongside a recording. created_by cannot tell them apart, so tasks now carry blind_requested, true only for the deliberate case; without it, narrowing the first guard would have achieved nothing.

nodes.label: Icons with no red, green, ticks or crosses, and never without their name
nodes.norm_label: icons with no red, green, ticks or crosses, and never without their name
nodes.rationale: Cards::Badge's palette is deliberately not borrowed: a badge says where evidence stands and these say nothing about evidence at all. The name appears beside the icon always, because an unlabelled symbol is exactly the thing that gets read as a judgement. Without JavaScript the icon is a plain link to the same definition, so the modal is a convenience and never the only way to read it.

nodes.label: Stage 31 — The rules on the wire, not in the skill (implemented)
nodes.norm_label: stage 31 — the rules on the wire, not in the skill (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Owner request: reinstalling a connector after every rule change is unrealistic in production. MCP has no "fetch the rules from a URL" mechanism because the server is already that URL, so the answer is one source served over the two live channels — every tool result, and GET /api/v1/guidance — with the skill carrying none of it.

nodes.label: The thin skill points rather than repeats
nodes.norm_label: the thin skill points rather than repeats
nodes.rationale: Cut from ~12 KB to 3.2 KB, keeping only what cannot arrive in a result — what Galedra is, the galedra: trigger, search first — and saying that where the skill and the live guidance differ, the guidance wins. Two rules are repeated anyway (your own reasoning is never evidence; never record claims about identifiable private individuals) because an assistant can break both before its first tool call and both damage the record rather than merely producing a worse answer. A spec fails if an operational rule migrates back.

nodes.label: Guidance::VERSION is advisory, never enforced
nodes.rationale: It tells a host showing guidance to a person whether their copy is current. No tool refuses a call because an assistant last read an older version; that would punish the assistant for the host's caching.

nodes.label: The write link: a knowingly non-standard GET, later removed
nodes.norm_label: the write link: a knowingly non-standard get, later removed
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/investigations/record recorded a bundle passed as base64url JSON because the alternative for a browsing-only assistant was a copy-and-paste step that loses the very users it was for; it was made acceptable by a required revocable token, idempotent receipts and filtered logs, then went tokenless, and was finally removed on the owner's instruction as a state-changing GET a crawler could trigger, needing no credential, for a host whose browser refused long URLs. Hosted assistants use OAuth over MCP instead.

nodes.label: ChatGPT connector interop fixes (OpenID discovery, RFC 9207, plain form submit)
nodes.norm_label: chatgpt connector interop fixes (openid discovery, rfc 9207, plain form submit)
nodes.rationale: Found by watching the log: ChatGPT fetches /.well-known/openid-configuration first, requires authorization_response_iss_parameter_supported and client_id_metadata_document_supported, and verifies iss before exchanging a code (RFC 9207); the consent form was submitted by Turbo, which cannot follow a cross-site redirect, so approvals went nowhere until it became a plain page submission.

nodes.label: Galedra as OAuth 2.1 authorization server for its own MCP endpoint
nodes.norm_label: galedra as oauth 2.1 authorization server for its own mcp endpoint
nodes.rationale: RFC 8414 and RFC 9728 metadata on the same host, RFC 7591 dynamic registration, S256-only PKCE, single-use ten-minute codes bound to client, redirect URI, challenge, scope and resource; refresh rotates and a replayed refresh token revokes its family. Tokens are stored as digests.

nodes.label: Acceptance rules and auto-ACCEPT
nodes.rationale: Acceptance is a system-signed ACCEPT appended in the same transaction for a human's own direct objects, but never for SET_TRUTH_EVALUABLE and never by the same principal for extraction proposals, cross-principal supersessions and merges, so no contributor can certify its own interpretive work.

nodes.label: Merges, supersessions, and evaluability derived from windows
nodes.norm_label: merges, supersessions, and evaluability derived from windows
nodes.rationale: Nothing rewrites the affected row: a merge or a supersession is an accepted, active windowed row, so INVALIDATE-ing it reverses the effect with no row restoration, which is what 02 SS3.3 promises; cached columns are recomputed by Projections::Refresh and rebuilt by replay, and *_at(seq) methods answer history.

nodes.label: Source content carried in the CREATE_SOURCE payload
nodes.norm_label: source content carried in the create_source payload
nodes.rationale: Keeping the text in the signed payload makes the log self-contained (a mirror of GET /log rebuilds every source) and makes replay trivial; content_hash is over UTF-8 bytes and CHAR_RANGE offsets are Unicode code points. 11 SS8 names Active Storage, deferred to a binary-source import flow.

nodes.label: Audit sampling runs inside Ledger::Apply, not as a job
nodes.norm_label: audit sampling runs inside ledger::apply, not as a job
nodes.rationale: 05 SS9 makes the sampling inputs a function of the log at the contribution's own seq, so computing and storing them during Apply is the only way replay reproduces every schedule row byte for byte; the planned ScheduleAuditJob was therefore unnecessary, and outcome_is_unusual is judged under the default model as of that seq so a later model release cannot change past decisions.

nodes.label: Challenged contributions do not count until confirmed
nodes.norm_label: challenged contributions do not count until confirmed
nodes.rationale: Audits::Status derives, as of any seq, whether a compromise window or a latest-UNRESOLVED audit covers a contribution with no later CONFIRMED audit, and Scoring::BuildInput drops such links, so doubt suppresses evidence rather than silently discounting it.

nodes.label: Reputation is audit-derived and not a scoring input
nodes.norm_label: reputation is audit-derived and not a scoring input
nodes.rationale: Beta(1,1) prior with the 05 SS7 deltas, computed from events active at a snapshot and bucketed per task type and domain, with limited history flagged under n < 3; the endpoint states that reputation is not authority, and it never enters a claim score (Invariant 8).

nodes.label: Re-audit restores by creating new rows
nodes.norm_label: re-audit restores by creating new rows
nodes.rationale: A disagreeing RE_AUDIT invalidates the first audit and its reputation event and the system appends an ACCEPT with basis RESTORED_AFTER_RE_AUDIT; Ledger::Restore recreates the invalidated rows as new rows with ids derived from the restoring ACCEPT and created_seq at that seq, so history shows the gap instead of hiding it.

nodes.label: Tie-break by created_seq before id
nodes.rationale: 03 SS4 Step 3 breaks equal magnitudes by lowest evidence id then link id, which assumes time-ordered ids; projection ids here are hash-derived, so the scorer input now carries each row's created_seq and compares it first, which is the order UUIDv7 ids would have given and what the reference scorer's integer handles encode.

nodes.label: ANONYMOUS identity tier
nodes.rationale: The spec's tiers start at pseudonymous; ANONYMOUS was added below it so someone with no account can still contribute. Anonymous work is weighted only where the constitution allows - a 3x audit sampling factor, a per-token daily cap and rate limit, and a provisional label naming the anonymous origin - and never in claim scores, which are byte-identical regardless of tier.

nodes.label: Galedra
nodes.rationale: An epistemic ledger exists because AI research is expensive to repeat and hard to audit; a durable, signed, reusable evidence record makes that work cumulative. It is deliberately not a source of truth but a source of traceable reasons for believing or doubting a claim.

nodes.label: Galeed (Genesis 31:47-48) naming origin
nodes.rationale: The cairn Jacob and Laban piled up: two parties, no shared authority, a durable marker left in the open. The name was chosen because the same shape applies to claims rather than covenants.

nodes.label: /weaknesses: where the ledger is most likely wrong
nodes.norm_label: /weaknesses: where the ledger is most likely wrong

nodes.label: The eighteen invariants any change must leave standing
nodes.norm_label: the eighteen invariants any change must leave standing
nodes.rationale: Condensed from 10-agent-handoff.md so a coding agent can check a change without re-reading the spec: log first, projections written only by Ledger::Apply, append-only, deterministic versioned scores, explicit unknown, no double counting, AI is never evidence by itself, reputation is not a scoring input, no self-certification.

nodes.label: Article I — Claims Are Not Truth
nodes.norm_label: article i — claims are not truth

nodes.label: Article XV — Shared Evidence and Personal Belief Are Separate Layers
nodes.norm_label: article xv — shared evidence and personal belief are separate layers

nodes.label: Article XVIII — Political Neutrality Is Structural
nodes.norm_label: article xviii — political neutrality is structural

nodes.label: Article XXI — Research Should Be Cumulative
nodes.norm_label: article xxi — research should be cumulative

nodes.label: Article XXII — The System Should Reveal Its Own Weaknesses
nodes.norm_label: article xxii — the system should reveal its own weaknesses

nodes.label: The Constitutional Test (ten questions)
nodes.rationale: A 'no' to questions 1, 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9, or a 'yes' to 3 or 4, requires written justification or a design change; the answers are recorded so a feature cannot quietly trade away traceability for convenience.

nodes.label: How a stage is executed
nodes.rationale: Each stage is a bounded unit of work ending in an annotated git tag, with every acceptance item covered by an automated test and a Decision Log entry written before the file moves from planned/ to implemented/. A stage is not done until its tag exists, and the next stage does not start until asked.

nodes.label: SettleLoneVerdictsJob schedule
nodes.rationale: Runs hourly at minute 30 in both production and development. It is the timer behind Reviews::Consensus settling a single uncontradicted verdict after 48 hours — the review outcome that has no second principal to agree with it still has to settle, and a periodic job is what makes the 48-hour rule take effect.

nodes.label: Audit sampling factors
nodes.rationale: base_rate 0.10 raised by multipliers: a new identity (first 10 contributions) by 5, low reliability (mean below 0.8) by 2, unusual activity by 2, and impact divided by 5. Sampling is risk-weighted rather than uniform.

nodes.label: RFC 8785 canonicalization subset and vectors
nodes.rationale: The client implements only the RFC 8785 subset the ledger uses: no floats, keys sorted by UTF-16 code units. spec/fixtures/canonical_json_vectors.json lets any client confirm it produces identical hashes, and Galedra::Jcs.canonical reproduces the same vectors on the server side — the shared vector file is what keeps independent implementations hash-compatible.

nodes.label: eir-result-v1 signed result envelope
nodes.rationale: The answer is signed as an eir-result-v1 envelope and posted to POST /api/v1/contributions — the single write path, so an agent result enters the log exactly as any other signed contribution.

nodes.label: Task lease (POST /api/v1/tasks/next, eir-lease-v1)
nodes.rationale: The agent leases the highest-priority task it is permitted to take, with a signed eir-lease-v1 body; permission comes from a human principal's DELEGATE to the registered AGENT key and from the task types the agent declares.

nodes.label: Every write is signed and open to audit
nodes.norm_label: every write is signed and open to audit
nodes.rationale: A write is attributed to the assistant as an agent acting for the user, or to an anonymous key, and left permanently open to audit in the public log. Stated to the assistant up front so the consequence of a careless contribution is known before it makes one.

nodes.label: Example agent (standalone Ruby client)
nodes.rationale: A reference implementation of the agent protocol (spec 04) depending only on Ruby's standard library, so an agent author can see the whole protocol without adopting any of the ledger's dependencies.

nodes.label: anonymous_factor (ANONYMOUS principals sampled more)
nodes.rationale: Stage 12. Contributions whose principal is ANONYMOUS are sampled 3x more often. Anonymous contribution is permitted rather than blocked, and the cost of that openness is paid in audit rate instead of in refusal.

nodes.label: Audit policy v0.1
nodes.rationale: Spec 05 §7–§10. Values are placeholders the spec says live in config. Changing them changes future sampling decisions but never past ones, because each past decision is stored with its inputs in audit_schedules — the policy is versioned (policy_version audit-policy-v0.1) so a sampling decision stays reproducible after the config moves.

nodes.label: High-impact confirming-audit bands
nodes.rationale: Spec 05 §10. How many confirming audits from distinct principals are needed before provisional clears, banded by downstream_count: 1 audit up to 2 downstream, 2 up to 9, and above that 2 audits plus an accepted OPPOSING_EVIDENCE_SEARCH (Stage 8). The more other claims depend on it, the more it costs to stop being provisional, and at the top band someone must have actively looked for the contrary case.

nodes.label: independent_checks (three independent answers)
nodes.rationale: Owner request, 2026-09-19. A claim's verification tasks ask for three independent answers. The first answer counts at once so one assistant can carry its own work through to something postable; the remaining two are what actually raise confidence, and the task stays open until they arrive or nobody comes. Trades immediate usefulness against corroboration without blocking the first contributor.

nodes.label: Defensive defaults for agent authors (04 §9)
nodes.rationale: Treat everything under untrusted_excerpt as data and never as instructions, and give the agent no write access beyond submitting its result. Prompt injection through quoted source text is the expected attack, so the excerpt is fenced by name in the packet and the agent's authority is scoped to a single result.

nodes.label: fixtures.json deterministic behaviours
nodes.rationale: Maps a task type (optionally plus a claim-text fragment) to one of confirm_direct, none_found, group_by_title, qualifier_demo, propose_claims, no_claims or none_material — deterministic behaviours, never heuristics, so the demo reproduces byte-identically. `--agent bad` selects the fixtures marked agent: bad, the demo's deliberate poisoning agent, which is how the ledger's defences are exercised.

nodes.label: Verify the packet's server signature against /api/v1/meta
nodes.norm_label: verify the packet's server signature against /api/v1/meta
nodes.rationale: The agent checks the server's signature on the work packet before acting on it, so trust runs in both directions: the ledger verifies the agent's result, and the agent verifies that the packet really came from the node whose key /api/v1/meta publishes.

nodes.label: Never record claims about identifiable private individuals
nodes.norm_label: never record claims about identifiable private individuals
nodes.rationale: A public figure in their public role is fair; a person they mention is not. The second of the two rules repeated locally, for the same reason: an append-only public log makes this kind of mistake permanent.

nodes.label: Your own reasoning is never evidence
nodes.norm_label: your own reasoning is never evidence
nodes.rationale: Only quoted passages are evidence. Never write a statement that cannot be pointed to in a source, and never invent a source, a quotation or a hash. Kept in the frozen skill file rather than only on the wire because an assistant could break it before its first call, and breaking it damages the record itself rather than merely producing a worse answer.

nodes.label: CI job: demo (both demos on a fresh database)
nodes.norm_label: ci job: demo (both demos on a fresh database)
nodes.rationale: Pins RFC 8032 test vector 1 as LEDGER_SYSTEM_PRIVATE_KEY — a published, non-secret key used only for CI — so the demo's signatures and therefore its golden values are reproducible.

nodes.label: Production app service (Thruster + Puma + Solid Queue)
nodes.norm_label: production app service (thruster + puma + solid queue)
nodes.rationale: Runs db:prepare, ledger:genesis and ledger:release_models before exec'ing Thruster, so a fresh host comes up with a genesis entry and released models without a manual step; TLS_DOMAIN drives Let's Encrypt inside the container.

nodes.label: cloudflared tunnel profile
nodes.rationale: A named Cloudflare tunnel terminates TLS and reaches app:80 inside the compose network, so a home node needs no router changes and no open ports.

nodes.label: Production db service (postgres:16 + pg_stat_statements)
nodes.rationale: pg_stat_statements is preloaded because it is how a running node answers 'which statement is costing us', which no Ruby profile can say.

nodes.label: Development app service
nodes.rationale: LEDGER_DEFAULT_MODEL is pinned to ledger-default@0.2.0 so releasing a newer model does not silently change what the node reports (Stage 35).

nodes.label: Deployment with Kamal 2
nodes.rationale: Kamal on a small cloud VM with managed PostgreSQL is the plan for the first public node, but config/deploy.yml does not exist yet; compose.production.yaml is what runs today and stays the fallback for a volunteer node.

nodes.label: Stack is decided; do not re-evaluate
nodes.norm_label: stack is decided; do not re-evaluate
nodes.rationale: Latest stable Ruby and Rails, PostgreSQL 16+, Solid Queue and Solid Cache, Hotwire, Ed25519, RFC 8785, RSpec, Docker Compose with exactly two services. Redis, Sidekiq, pgvector, a JS framework and any external service are out of P0 so the demo runs with no API key.

nodes.label: Exactly two services: app and db (spec 11 §2)
nodes.norm_label: exactly two services: app and db (spec 11 §2)
nodes.rationale: Puma runs the Solid Queue supervisor in-process (SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA), so web and jobs share one container and the deployment stays two services.

nodes.label: Why DigitalOcean first
nodes.rationale: Preferred over raw AWS EC2 for the first node because it exposes fewer infrastructure concepts while still providing ordinary Linux VMs, private networking and managed PostgreSQL; the first deployment optimizes for developer attention, predictable cost, simple operations, easy recovery and portability.

nodes.label: Guiding principle: the first host should be deliberately ordinary
nodes.norm_label: guiding principle: the first host should be deliberately ordinary
nodes.rationale: Complexity should be spent on the epistemic model, not cloud infrastructure; the infrastructure succeeds when it is boring, inexpensive, recoverable, portable, agent-operable and easy to replace.

nodes.label: Ruby and Rails: always the latest stable release
nodes.norm_label: ruby and rails: always the latest stable release
nodes.rationale: Stage 0 re-checks and pins; if Rails does not yet support the newest Ruby line, use the newest Ruby that Rails release supports and record it, rather than holding the whole stack back.

nodes.label: Topic: Culture
nodes.rationale: Scope note draws the distinction that a meme is a source, not a subject: this topic is for claims about culture itself, not for tagging the memes that carried them.

nodes.label: Topic: Health
nodes.rationale: Scope: personal and public health, nutrition, vaccines. Audit domain: health.

nodes.label: Topic: Law
nodes.rationale: Scope: courts and legislation. The scope line records the open question that no legal scoring model exists yet, which is one of the decisions reserved for the owner (whether LEGAL claims are scored before a legal model exists).

nodes.label: Topic: Mathematics
nodes.rationale: Scope: numbers, statistics, and quantitative reasoning. Audit domain: mathematics.

nodes.label: Topic vocabulary (closed, two levels)
nodes.rationale: IMPLEMENTATION.md Stage 15. The vocabulary is deliberately closed and only two levels deep so tags stay comparable across the ledger. A tag is a signed TAG_CLAIM contribution carrying a path like science/biology, never an edited column. Each top level names the audit/reputation domain it maps to; a child may override it. Adding or renaming a topic is a code change reviewed like any other; whether it should instead become a signed config release is reserved for the owner.

nodes.label: Portable Agent Memory
nodes.rationale: Converges independently on content addressing, cryptographic provenance and cross-model portability, but answers 'what does an agent remember' where the ledger asks 'why is this proposition warranted'.

nodes.label: Future Directions (deferred; not to be built in the POC)
nodes.norm_label: future directions (deferred; not to be built in the poc)
nodes.rationale: Exists so the coding agent can avoid decisions that would block these later, and so deferred items from earlier drafts have a documented home.

nodes.label: Galedra Federation Goal
nodes.rationale: Long-term architectural and governance direction, explicitly not a P0 requirement: federation should follow only after the core models prove useful on a single node.

nodes.label: Deferred from v0.1 (with reasons and compatibility hooks)
nodes.norm_label: deferred from v0.1 (with reasons and compatibility hooks)
nodes.rationale: Each deferred item names what must stay compatible — claim_edges with validity windows, the reserved CREATE_INFERENCE action, qualifiers JSONB, the independence_strategy config key — so deferral does not become a blocker.

nodes.label: Domain Interfaces on the Same Ledger
nodes.norm_label: domain interfaces on the same ledger

nodes.label: Open Governance Questions
nodes.rationale: Article XII's capture resistance ultimately depends on these answers more than on any code: the data license, who holds the system key, who appoints moderators, how model releases and amendments are approved.

nodes.label: Long-Term Vision — Organize Reasons for Belief the Way the Web Organized Documents
nodes.norm_label: long-term vision — organize reasons for belief the way the web organized documents

nodes.label: Mirroring and Federation
nodes.rationale: The graph should not depend forever on one operator.

nodes.label: Research Scheduler and Local-Agent Donations
nodes.rationale: Priority by expected discriminative value between hypotheses; opt-in donated idle compute returns signed results.

nodes.label: Specialized Scoring Models
nodes.rationale: All read the same log; communities may publish competing models and the graph does not fork.

nodes.label: Invariant 12 — Moderation Is Visible
nodes.rationale: Quarantine and takedown leave public stubs; nothing disappears without a trace.

nodes.label: Invariant 14 — More Than One Model
nodes.rationale: Scoring code must never assume a single model; the second model exists to keep that honest.

nodes.label: Article V — Contradiction Is Preserved
nodes.rationale: Disagreement is made legible through typed relationships rather than resolved by deleting inconvenient evidence or suppressing minority hypotheses.

nodes.label: Article XII — The System Must Resist Capture
nodes.norm_label: article xii — the system must resist capture
nodes.rationale: Assume powerful actors will try to manipulate the system; no operator should be able to silently rewrite its epistemic history.

nodes.label: Constitutional Test Q10 — Would we still want this mechanism in the hands of people we disagree with?
nodes.norm_label: constitutional test q10 — would we still want this mechanism in the hands of people we disagree with?

nodes.label: Anti-Capture Goal
nodes.rationale: Governance does not disappear; it becomes inspectable, plural and technically difficult to monopolize.

nodes.label: Asymmetric Storage Participation
nodes.rationale: Full archival, domain, replica, index, personal and institutional node classes: the federation should benefit from heterogeneous participation rather than requiring identical servers.

nodes.label: Conflicts Are Preserved
nodes.rationale: A merge conflict in epistemic content is often information, not merely a technical problem to overwrite.

nodes.label: Peer and Shard Discovery
nodes.rationale: Do not choose a mechanism before real federation requirements are known.

nodes.label: Guiding Vision — The Distributed Cairn
nodes.rationale: No stone is the monument by itself; overlapping custody makes the record harder to erase or silently rewrite.

nodes.label: Eventual Consistency Over Global Locking
nodes.rationale: A volunteer global network cannot depend on one global lock, one leader, constant connectivity or one trusted timestamp server.

nodes.label: Failure and Recovery
nodes.rationale: No critical public claim should depend indefinitely on a single origin server; reconstructibility should become a measurable network property.

nodes.label: Federation Charter
nodes.rationale: Running compatible software does not make a node a recognized member, and membership grants no epistemic authority.

nodes.label: Globally Durable Object Identity
nodes.rationale: A record must not be identified solely by a node's database row, because that node may disappear; content-addressable identity lets any node verify two copies are the same object.

nodes.label: Licensing Separation — AGPL / Apache-2.0 / ODbL / CC0
nodes.norm_label: licensing separation — agpl / apache-2.0 / odbl / cc0
nodes.rationale: Licenses protect openness; operational cooperation belongs in the Federation Charter rather than in a license.

nodes.label: Foundational Principle — No Node Is the Truth Authority
nodes.norm_label: foundational principle — no node is the truth authority
nodes.rationale: A node is a custodian, participant, verifier and replica; the originating node does not become authoritative merely because it created the contribution, and the graph must survive the loss of its origin.

nodes.label: POC Non-Goal — Do Not Implement Federation Now
nodes.norm_label: poc non-goal — do not implement federation now
nodes.rationale: Building it before validating the epistemic data model would spend effort on the wrong uncertainty; the POC must merely avoid decisions that make federation unnecessarily difficult later.

nodes.label: Protocol Is More Important Than the Reference Implementation
nodes.norm_label: protocol is more important than the reference implementation
nodes.rationale: The success condition is that independent implementations can participate in the same epistemic commons, not that everyone runs the Rails application.

nodes.label: Public and Private Data Must Remain Distinguishable
nodes.norm_label: public and private data must remain distinguishable
nodes.rationale: The architecture must never require publication of private material merely because a federation-compatible node processed it.

nodes.label: Replication Across Administrative Domains
nodes.rationale: Minimum replicas and minimum administrative domains are examples, not current requirements.

nodes.label: Shards, Subgraphs and Collections — Not a Strict Tree
nodes.norm_label: shards, subgraphs and collections — not a strict tree
nodes.rationale: The same atomic claim supports multiple documents, hypotheses and arguments, so federation units must not assume tree ownership; the partitioning strategy should be learned from real usage.

nodes.label: Signed Checkpoints
nodes.rationale: Lets other nodes attest they hold a verified replica, which makes replication measurable rather than assumed.

nodes.label: Federation P0 — Single Node
nodes.rationale: Prove the data model, deterministic replay, scoring, provenance and single-team workflows; no distributed-systems complexity is justified yet.

nodes.label: Federation P1 — Independent Mirrors
nodes.rationale: Primarily about durability, not distributed write coordination.

nodes.label: Federation P2 — Specialized Nodes
nodes.rationale: A node does not need the entire global graph to participate.

nodes.label: Federation P3 — Cross-Replication
nodes.rationale: Important public shards should exist on multiple administratively independent nodes, resilient to abandonment, censorship and funding loss.

nodes.label: Federation P4 — Confederated Network
nodes.rationale: The original Galedra server becomes one participant among many.

nodes.label: Volunteer Economics — Net Contribution Value
nodes.rationale: Federation should not equate raw volume with contribution quality; a low-quality contributor can create more audit burden than value.

nodes.label: Open Questions for the Project Owner
nodes.norm_label: open questions for the project owner
nodes.rationale: Adoption of P-1 through P-4, the data license, who holds the system key, whether LEGAL claims are scored, and whether TEXTUAL stays a distinct claim type.

nodes.label: Audit Economics
nodes.rationale: Volunteer AI compute is not automatically valuable: a low-quality agent may create more audit work than useful knowledge, so scheduling should net out audit and correction cost.

nodes.label: Single database, Solid Queue inside Puma
nodes.norm_label: single database, solid queue inside puma
nodes.rationale: 11 SS2 requires one PostgreSQL database, so the Solid installers' separate schemas were folded into one migration and the production multi-database connects_to wiring removed; Solid Queue runs in Puma via the plugin so the app service stays one container and one process tree.

nodes.label: Cross-implementation test vectors
nodes.rationale: Expected canonical bytes and hashes were generated by an independent Python script rather than by the Ruby code, so the implementation is checked against a second one as 04 SS11 intends; RFC 8785 and RFC 8032 published vectors pin the rest.

nodes.label: json gem pinned to 2.x
nodes.rationale: Ruby 4.0.7 bundles json 3.0.2 whose JSON.parse takes keyword-only options, while ActiveSupport 8.1.3.1 passes a positional hash, so every jsonb read and JSON body raised ArgumentError and the schema dumper silently omitted the contributors table; pinning 2.21.2 keeps both Ruby 4.0.7 and Rails 8.1.3.1 in place until the next Rails patch.

nodes.label: UUIDv7 primary keys assigned in Ruby
nodes.norm_label: uuidv7 primary keys assigned in ruby
nodes.rationale: Postgres 16 has no native uuidv7(), so ids are assigned by an ApplicationRecord callback and the migration sets no database default, making a silent v4 id impossible; the Rails auth tables keep bigint ids because they are not ledger tables.

nodes.label: eir-export-v1 — a byte-identical, node-signed bundle
nodes.rationale: bundle_hash is over the body in RFC 8785 canonical form and the header is signed by the system key following eir-checkpoint-v1, so a mirror can tell a file came from the node it names, intact, without asking that node anything, and two nodes holding one subject can be compared by hash. Compact states verifiable: false in its own header, because a reader who cannot check something should be told by the file rather than by a footnote.

nodes.label: Stage 14 - MCP, OpenAPI, and the skill
nodes.norm_label: stage 14 - mcp, openapi, and the skill

nodes.label: ADOPT_KEY proves control of both keys
nodes.norm_label: adopt_key proves control of both keys
nodes.rationale: Anonymous work can be put under an account later: the adopter's human key signs and the adopted key counter-signs {adopt, key_id}, so the contribution itself proves control of both. The adopted key keeps its own rows and reputation buckets and contributor pages show the link both ways; audit schedules already computed keep their stored inputs.

nodes.label: OpenAI-shaped search and fetch tools
nodes.rationale: GPT creation left personal accounts and GPTs retire, with MCP plugins as the replacement, so two read-only tools named search and fetch were added for hosts that only allow read-and-fetch connectors, every tool got an outputSchema, and annotations mark reads read-only and writes idempotent. ChatGPT's browser strips long URLs, which is why the write link could never serve a plain chat.

nodes.label: MCP served by Rails itself
